_about: Subjective view per upcoming match, keyed by ESPN match id, written by a scheduled task from recent news. Shown in each stat's 'Why' box and next to 'Our call'; never mixed into the numbers. Per stat (goals, corners, cards, shots, shots_on_target): {lean: higher|lower|same, call: short judgement call, text: reasoning}. Also: overall, sources (URLs), written_at (ISO). Never use 'lock', 'sure thing' or 'guaranteed'.

401884736.overall: Bayern are top with 21 points from nine games, level on points with second place, and host 15th-placed Cologne, who have won one of their last five. Vincent Kompany is back in charge after his collapse in October and took Thursday's press conference: Musiala will probably be in the squad after his thigh tear (a start is not ruled out, most likely a bench role), while Luis Díaz is 'still a bit too soon' and should be back within a week; Neuer, Gnabry, Saibari and Davies (new hamstring tear) are also out, and the numbers already count all of these as missing. Cologne, under René Wagner, are without van den Berg, Hübers, Dallinga, Rondic and Skhiri (all counted); striker Ragnar Ache is fit and in the squad but may not start. The referee on file is Robin Braun, whose card record the numbers already use.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and already take about 12% off Bayern's attack for Díaz and Musiala as fully out. Kompany confirmed Díaz misses this one, so that part holds, but Musiala will probably be in the squad and could get minutes, which the numbers don't see; I nudge up only 1% (about 3.74), down from 2% yesterday now that Díaz is ruled out. Cologne's attack without Dallinga and Skhiri is already counted, and Ache returning on the bench is too small to move it.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, with Bayern's recent run (37 corners in six) already in them. Wagner expects Bayern to 'pin us back into our own half' and wants his side to defend with passion, which is the deep-block game the numbers already expect, so I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, and they already add about 9% for referee Robin Braun (4.4 cards a game against a 3.9 average) and Cologne's high recent card count (17 in six). A one-sided game where Cologne defend deep can bring tactical fouls, but nothing in the news goes beyond what is already counted, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 32.0 shots and already add 7.5% for Bayern's hot shooting run (127 shots in six). Bayern's attack around Kane and Olise is near full strength apart from Díaz, who is counted, and Cologne getting Ache back mostly helps them on the break, too little to change the total, so I stay at 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.4 shots on target, already lifted 11% for Bayern's recent accuracy. Musiala off the bench adds a little, but that is already reflected in the small goals nudge, and Cologne's attack without Dallinga is counted, so I stay at 12.4.

401884732.overall: Union are 16th and winless in four; Leipzig are 4th with four wins in five and host Lens in the Champions League three days later, so some rotation is possible (Starting11 notes they already keep only 60% of their XI). Union's week has gone badly: Ligainsider and Comunio report top scorer Janik Haberer resting with illness and Trimmel, Uduokhai and Burcu missing training or carrying knocks, none of which the numbers know. Leipzig miss Guiu, Ouédraogo and Finkgräfe (counted) plus defender Esteve (one tracker). No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower by 5%, to about 2.85: Union's top scorer Haberer is ill and Burcu missed training (Ligainsider, Comunio), on top of an attack that has already struggled (48 shots in six), and Leipzig may rotate before Lens. Neither is on the numbers' list; Union's poor form is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already cut for both sides' low recent corner counts (Union 18, Leipzig 22 in six). Rotation and Union's absences do not clearly push corners either way, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already add Union's rough recent run (18 cards in six). No referee is named; Uduokhai and Trimmel being doubtful changes who defends for Union but gives no clear reason for more or fewer cards, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.1 shots and already cut Union's shots 13% for their recent drought. I go 4% lower, to about 24.1, because Haberer's illness and Burcu's absence thin Union further and a rotated Leipzig front line before the Champions League may take a little volume out.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Same reasons as shots: Union lose their top scorer to illness and Leipzig may rotate before Lens, so I go 4% lower, to about 8.9. Leipzig's recent accuracy (+8%) is already counted.

401884735.overall: Leverkusen are 5th and host Paderborn, 13th with one loss in five. Leverkusen's forward line is badly hit: besides Diaby (counted), injury trackers list Kofane, Ben Seghir, Terrier and Tella out and defender Bade too, and only Diaby's absence moves the numbers' goals. Paderborn miss Hoffmeier, Klaas, Batista Meier, Awortwie-Grant and Gayret (listed) plus forward S. Michel (one tracker). Starting11 notes Leverkusen rotate a lot (60% of the XI kept); no referee is named yet, and I found no dedicated preview for this match after searching, so team news rests on injury trackers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and take only about 3% off for Diaby. Two trackers also list forwards Kofane, Ben Seghir and Terrier out, which the numbers' missing list does not, and Leverkusen have scored only 8 in six (partly counted through momentum), so I lean lower by 5%, to about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.4 corners, with Leverkusen expected to have most of the ball against a deep Paderborn side. The forward absences change who finishes moves more than how often Leverkusen attack down the flanks, so I stay at 11.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. No referee is named and nothing suggests a heated game; Paderborn's lower recent card count is already counted, so I stay at 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, already lifted slightly for both sides' recent volume. Leverkusen have kept shooting a lot (102 in six) despite the injuries, so the absences hurt quality more than volume and I stay at 31.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. With Kofane, Ben Seghir and Terrier out and not on the numbers' list, Leverkusen's finishing is weaker, so I go 3% lower, to about 10.0.

401884731.overall: Bottom side Gladbach (4 points, one win in nine) host Dortmund, 2nd and level on points with Bayern. Gladbach are badly depleted: Itakura is banned, Bolin and Ullrich are out (counted), and trackers also list Kühn, Kleindienst, Honorat, Fleck and goalkeeper Nicolas out or doubtful. Dortmund miss Can, Konstantelias and Lerma (counted), Ryerson came off hurt on international duty (one report), and they play in the Champions League three days later, so Starting11 expects some rotation. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, already taking Bolin and Ullrich off Gladbach's attack. I lean 3% lower, to about 2.7: Kühn, Kleindienst and Honorat are also missing or doubtful, and Dortmund may rotate before their Champions League game; Kühn and Kleindienst have been out since October, so their absence is partly in recent form already, hence the small size.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners, already nudged up for Dortmund's recent count (37 in six). Nothing in the news points either way for corners, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards and already add a big 22% for Gladbach's recent card spike (21 in six), with Itakura's ban after a yellow-red part of that story. No referee is named; I do not add more on top, so I stay at 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.2 shots, already lifted for both sides' recent shooting. Gladbach's thin attack and a possibly rotated Dortmund ahead of the Champions League point a little lower, so I go 3% down, to about 27.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Same reasons as shots: Gladbach without several forwards and Dortmund possibly rotating, so I go 3% lower, to about 9.3.

401884734.overall: Frankfurt (10th) and Hoffenheim (9th) are level on 12 points, so it is a mid-table game with little extra at stake. Frankfurt miss the banned Elias Baum and Götze (counted). Hoffenheim's defence is stretched: Hajdari, Hranáč and Gendrey are out (listed), Starting11 says Kabak is banned after three yellow cards, and another tracker lists Prass suspended and Coufal injured; none of those three is in the numbers. Conté's absence up front is counted. No referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals. I lean higher by 5%, to about 3.8: Hoffenheim are short at the back, with Kabak banned (Starting11) and Prass and Coufal listed out (buli-tipphilfe), on top of Hajdari, Hranáč and Gendrey, and the numbers give Frankfurt no lift for any of it. Each report is single-source, so the size stays mild.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners, already nudged up for Hoffenheim's recent count. A reshuffled Hoffenheim defence may concede more chances but not clearly more corners, so I stay at 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, with recent counts and head-to-head already in them. No referee is named; makeshift defenders can pick up fouls, but that is a hunch, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots and already add Hoffenheim's recent volume (101 in six, +12%). The absences in Hoffenheim's defence affect chance quality more than total shots, so I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target. With Hoffenheim missing Kabak and possibly Prass and Coufal, Frankfurt should get cleaner looks, so I go 3% higher, to about 10.4.

401884728.overall: Promoted Elversberg (7th, 13 pts) host Freiburg (3rd, 19 pts) in the first Bundesliga meeting between the clubs. Elversberg's games under Vincent Wagner have been wild (4-3 v Augsburg, 4-1 v Mainz, 0-4 at Leipzig, 1-2 at Dortmund), while Julian Schuster's Freiburg won four of their last five, including 1-0 at Trabzonspor in the Europa League. Elversberg miss defenders Pinckert and Gyamerah (both counted by the numbers), Tom Zimmerschied was due back mid-November and FotMob lists Noah Darvich as doubtful; Freiburg are without Florent Muslija (counted) and young full-back Berkay Yilmaz, banned after a red card, but he has not started a game this season. Keeper Mio Backhaus left the Germany U21 squad with a hand/thumb problem and is back in training, so he looks set to play. No referee has been named; news on Elversberg was fairly thin, so most stats stay with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already high, and they count Elversberg missing defenders Pinckert and Gyamerah (about +6% each on Freiburg's goals). Elversberg's high-scoring games fit that figure, Freiburg's goalkeeper Backhaus is back in training after his hand injury, and Yilmaz's ban hardly matters as he is not a starter, so I stay at about 3.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, with Freiburg's recent run of corners (30 in six) already added (+3%). Freiburg's wide play through Beste and Treu gets them most of the corners and Elversberg concede plenty, but that is what the numbers already see; I found nothing new, so about 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards. No referee has been named, and neither side's recent card counts stand out beyond the small momentum moves already made; Wagner's touchline ban earlier in the season is over. Nothing points either way, so I stay at about 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with Freiburg (16) expected to shoot more than the hosts. Elversberg have allowed 103 shots in their last six and Freiburg have been shooting above their usual level; both are already in the numbers' momentum, so I keep about 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target. Elversberg's open games and Freiburg's slightly below-par accuracy lately (23 on target in six, already counted) balance out, and no lineup news changes the attacks, so I stay at about 8.4.

401884729.overall: Schalke (17th, one win in nine) host Stuttgart (8th, three wins in five) after the international break. Miron Muslic's side defend well for a promoted team but create very little; Gosens, Wöber, Schallenberg and Bachmann are out (counted), Timo Becker is doubtful rather than ruled out, and striker Moussa Sylla is back in full training, likely as a sub. Stuttgart's playmaker Angelo Stiller has been out since an adductor injury in late October and, per LigaInsider citing the Stuttgarter Nachrichten, trained only individually on Monday, so a comeback at Schalke looks unlikely; he is not on the brief's missing list. Vagnoman and Sauer are close to returning to training (both counted as out) and Diehl is out long-term. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off for Gosens and Wöber at Schalke and Vagnoman at Stuttgart. I lean a little lower: Stiller, who sets up much of Stuttgart's play, is likely still out and the numbers don't list him, while Schalke have scored only 2 in six and Sylla probably starts on the bench. 2.1 x 0.95 gives about 2.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, with Stuttgart expected to win most of them. Schalke sit deep and counter, which hands the visitors corners, but that is already in both sides' records; Stiller's absence does not change Stuttgart's wing play, so about 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.3 cards, with a small momentum bump for Schalke. A desperate home side that presses can pick up fouls, but no referee has been named and neither side's recent card record is unusual, so I stay at about 3.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.9 shots. Schalke's attack has produced too few shots and box entries all season (as 90min notes) and Stuttgart lose their main midfield passer Stiller, which the numbers don't list; a mild trim gives about 27.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target and already cut Schalke's for their poor recent accuracy (13 on target in six). Without Stiller, Stuttgart's chances are likely a bit poorer, so I trim to about 9.2.

401884733.overall: Two struggling sides: Augsburg (14th) are seven games without a win under Manuel Baum and were pulled apart 5-2 at Leipzig before the break, having thrown away a 1-0 lead six times this season; Mainz (12th) have lost four in a row, the last 2-1 to Bayern, and still have no home win under Urs Fischer. Augsburg lose defender Chrislain Matsima, hurt in training (counted by the numbers), while Mainz get Stefan Posch and Phillipp Mwene back from the suspensions they served against Bayern. Mainz remain without midfielder Dominik Kohr (operated, out until January) and Silas. Mainz won the last two meetings 2-0 and 4-1. News this week was fairly thin (club team pages had not been updated since late October), and no referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already high: they add momentum for both leaky defences (+4% each) and Matsima's absence for Mainz (+6%). Augsburg conceded 17 in six and Mainz 16, and Posch's return should steady Mainz a little, so I see no reason to move from about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, Augsburg expected to win slightly more at home. Nothing in the news changes either side's wide play, and the small momentum and head-to-head moves are already made, so about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards, with momentum and head-to-head adding for Mainz. I trim slightly because Dominik Kohr, Mainz's combative holding midfielder, is out until January after surgery, and the numbers' three-year record still carries his seasons; Mainz have been booked often even without him, so only -3, about 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, already lifted by Augsburg's big recent volume (+19% momentum) and Mainz's shot count (+7%). Both teams play open games, which that figure already reflects, so I stay at about 31.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with momentum adding for both (+13% Augsburg, +6% Mainz). Two weak defences point the same way as the numbers already do, so I keep about 10.8.

401884730.overall: The 111th Nordderby: Daniel Thioune's Werder (6th, 15 pts) host Merlin Polzin's Hamburg (11th, 12 pts), the first time since 2012 both come in this high. Werder lost 1-0 at Stuttgart but have won three of four at home and eight of the last nine home league meetings with HSV; Hamburg beat Gladbach 3-1 with long-range goals from Muheim and Grønbæk. Werder are without Weiser (thigh, counted), Musah and Topp, while Grüll is in the Bundesliga's predicted lineup; Hamburg miss Poulsen (counted, -12% on their goals), Remberg and Nadir, and Sambi Lokonga, listed out until December, appears in the predicted lineup. The derby effect is already a big +39% on cards. Fresh team news was thin (no club press conferences yet), so the view rests on the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals and already take off for Weiser at Werder and Poulsen and Sambi Lokonga at Hamburg. If Sambi Lokonga plays, as the Bundesliga's predicted lineup suggests, Hamburg's attack gets back a little, but that is not confirmed, so I stay at about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with Werder expected to win most at home. Hamburg's three-at-the-back shape with wing-backs Muheim and El Ouahdi is already in their record, and nothing in the news changes it, so about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.9 cards, already including the derby boost (+39%) and head-to-head from past meetings. Both sides have been booked less than usual lately (counted), and no referee is named, so I do not add more: about 5.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.2 shots, lifted by Werder's strong recent volume (+20% momentum). Hamburg tend to sit in a back three away from home and let Werder have the ball, which that figure already reflects, so I keep about 31.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, with Werder's 43 on target in six already added (+15%). I found no lineup news that changes either attack, so I stay at about 10.8.

401883112.overall: A relegation fight in Encamp on Friday night: FC Andorra are 21st with 11 points and one draw in their last four, Leganés 16th with 15 after a 3-1 win over Burgos, their first under Luis Carrión. Andorra are without goalkeeper Jesús Owono (12-match ban after the Tenerife collision that led to Jesús de Miguel's death) and centre-back Diego Alende (red card at Almería), both already in the numbers, plus midfielder Théo Le Normand (injured); Gael Alonso, Efe Akman and Lauti De León are back, and Bomba is in the probable XI, so the worry about a makeshift centre-back pair in my earlier view has eased. Carles Manso wants a reaction after conceding early goals and a penalty in each of the last three games, and says Carrión has made Leganés keep the ball more. Leganés get Javi Montero back from a ban and Diawara and Gharbi back from international duty; José Luis Guzmán Mansilla referees, and the numbers already count his low card record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already add about 6% to Leganés' goals for Alende's ban. My earlier small lean higher rested on Bomba being doubtful, but Infobae's preview has him starting next to Lautaro Spatz and Gael Alonso is back in the squad, so I drop it and stay at 2.8. Andorra have conceded 24 in 13 and Manso admits they give away early goals and penalties, while Leganés scored three in half an hour against Burgos; all of that is already in their records and recent form.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, 5.8 of them Andorra's, as a home side that usually has the ball and pushes up. Manso says Leganés keep the ball more under Carrión, which could trim Andorra's share a little, but Leganés' recent habit of conceding corners is already in momentum (+3.9%), so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards: both sides have been booked a lot lately (+11% and +6.6% momentum) and the referee, José Luis Guzmán Mansilla, averages 4.7 cards a game, which already takes about 13% off. It is a tense relegation game, but nothing I read points to extra needle beyond that, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, about 18 of them Andorra's, which assumes Leganés sit deep. Manso said Carrión's Leganés now keep more of the ball and attack with few passes, so Andorra may get fewer long spells of pressure; that is one coach's view, so I only trim a little, to about 26.4. Leganés' high shots conceded lately are already in momentum (+7%).

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, with Andorra's recent accuracy already in momentum (+7.4%). I had added a little for a patched-up Andorra defence, but with Bomba expected to start and Gael Alonso back that reason is gone, and the slightly lower shot count is too small to move this, so I stay at 9.6.

401882299.overall: Granada arrive in top form: since this brief's table they beat Las Palmas 1-0 on Sunday for a sixth straight league win, with Pacheta's side pressing high and attacking down the wings, though Casadesús and Owen (Spain U17) are out and Diallo and Arnaiz were due back this week. Sabadell (14th, five league games without a win, unbeaten at home but with four 0-0 draws) are in an injury crisis: two outlets list nine players out for Ferran Costa (Bonaldo, Urri, Quadri, Eneko, Pipa, Codina, Nuamah, Xavi Moreno and Gioacchini), plus Català's red-card ban. The numbers only know about Gioacchini and Català, so the other absences are new to them. Sabadell also played a Copa del Rey tie at Utebo on Wednesday evening with a short squad (14 fit outfield players by one count), so tired legs are likely; no referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals, already taking off Gioacchini (-13.5% on Sabadell) and adding Granada's run through momentum. Sabadell's wider injury list should cut their own scoring further, but a tired, patched-up side also gives Granada more room, and Sabadell's home games have been tight (four 0-0 draws this season); those pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 1.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.4 corners, most of them Sabadell's (4.9). I trim to about 8.1 because with eight absentees beyond those the numbers count and a Copa game in their legs, Sabadell are less likely to sustain the wide pressure their corner count relies on, and Granada's recent low corner count is already in momentum (-2.9%).

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards; Sabadell's slightly busier booking lately and Granada's clean recent record are both already in momentum. Fatigue can bring late fouls, but Granada usually sit on leads with few bookings and no referee is named yet, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.1 shots, with Sabadell taking 17. I lean lower, to about 25.7, because Sabadell have eight more players out that the numbers don't know about (only Gioacchini and Català are counted), including Bonaldo, who went off injured at Eldense, plus a Copa tie on Wednesday; Granada's pressing should keep the home side's volume down more than it adds to their own.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target. I trim slightly, to about 7.6, for the same reason as shots: Sabadell's depleted, tired attack has already been inaccurate lately (17 on target in six games, which the numbers count), and Granada's finishing has been patchy even while winning.

401883108.overall: A bottom-of-the-table six-pointer at Zubieta: Real Sociedad II are 18th with 13 points and Cádiz 20th with 11 after a point at Eibar, with Borja Jiménez's position being discussed (the Cádiz president publicly asked for time for him). Sanse miss Jon Balda through suspension, which the numbers count. New to the numbers: Cádiz's regular left-back Sergio Arribas is banned after his fifth yellow card (RFEF list and a Cádiz paper agree), with Cristian Gutiérrez expected in, and Portal Cadista reports another defensive setback; Rivera, Orellana and Tabatadze remain out as the brief says. Both sides foul a lot (Sanse have committed 246 fouls, Cádiz have 44 yellows), and no referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already moving for Balda's ban on both sides. I lean slightly higher, about 2.8, because Cádiz lose starting left-back Sergio Arribas to suspension, which the numbers don't know, and another defensive setback was reported; Sanse have been shooting a lot lately and Cádiz have conceded in most games.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, and Real Sociedad II's recent jump in corners (38 in six) is already in momentum (+8.8%). Arribas' absence could open the Cádiz left flank a little, but that is too small to size, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards. I add a little, to about 5.4: it is a relegation six-pointer between two sides that foul and get booked a lot (Sanse 246 fouls committed, Cádiz 44 yellows, Borja Vázquez one card from a ban), and the brief carries no stakes adjustment; losing booking-prone Arribas takes a bit off, and no referee is named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, with the young home side taking about 18; their recent shooting surge is already added (+18.9% momentum) and Cádiz's low shot output is in too (-9%). I found nothing on rotation or style that changes this, so I stay at 27.2.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. In line with goals, I add a little, to about 8.5, as a reshuffled Cádiz back line without Arribas should let Sanse get a few more efforts on target; Sanse's recent accuracy is already in momentum (+1.7%).

401882301.overall: Castellón are 2nd with 30 points, nine wins from 13 and the league's best defence (5 conceded), and won 1-0 at Valladolid last weekend; Suero leads them with six goals and Brignani's long injury is already in the numbers. Eldense (15th, 17 points) under Javi Calleja beat ten-man Sabadell 2-0 on Sunday, get Juan Larios back from suspension, and were still without Guille Macho as of last weekend. Eldense are the more booked side (37 yellows to Castellón's 25), which the numbers already weigh heavily through momentum. News was thin: I found no match preview, injury update for Castellón or referee yet, so the view rests on form and season stats.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, mostly Castellón's (2.0) against an Eldense side that has conceded 19 and scored 15. Castellón's tight defence and Suero's scoring are already in the ratings, and Larios' return for Eldense is too small to move it, so I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Castellón keep the ball (over 7,000 passes, the most of these sides) and should pin Eldense back, but Eldense's low recent corner count is already in momentum (-5.6%), and I found no lineup news to change it, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, with Eldense's busy recent booking already adding +16.8% on their side; they have 37 yellows this season to Castellón's 25. No referee has been named and nothing points to extra needle, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.5 shots; both sides have taken a similar number this season (132 and 134) and Castellón's slightly quieter recent shooting is in momentum (-5.1%). With no injury or rotation news found for either side, I stay at 24.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Castellón's dip in accuracy over the last six games is already counted (-5.6%), and nothing I found changes either side's attack, so I stay at 8.7.

401883107.overall: Tenerife (13th, 18 points) are still grieving forward Jesús de Miguel, who died after the 2 November game with Andorra; in their first match since, Álvaro Cervera's side beat Ceuta 2-0, and captain Enric Gallego (eight goals) carries their attack. Goalkeeper Dani Martín, banned for that game, should be back, and Ranos and Dani Fernández have returned from international duty, while Baba was still recovering. Mallorca are 7th with 23 points and the stronger defence (10 conceded) but drew 3-3 with Córdoba last time out; Morlanes and Jan Salas are out and already in the numbers. News was thin: I found no Mallorca team-news page or match preview yet, and no referee is named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals. Tenerife rely heavily on Gallego and drew four in a row before beating Ceuta, while Mallorca concede little but just let in three against Córdoba; both runs are already in momentum, and Morlanes' absence is counted, so I stay at 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, fairly even between the sides. Mallorca's big recent corner count (43 in six) is already added through momentum (+5%), and I found no lineup or style news to change it, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.6 cards, already lifted by both sides' recent bookings (+5.9% and +8.8%); Mallorca have 37 yellows this season to Tenerife's 30. The Heliodoro will be emotional, but that cuts both ways and no referee is named, so I stay at 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 22.5 shots; Mallorca shoot more (121 to Tenerife's 101 this season) and their recent volume is in momentum. With Tenerife's internationals back and no rotation news found for Mallorca, I stay at 22.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 6.7 shots on target. Tenerife's attack runs through Gallego and their recent low accuracy is counted (-1.2%); I found nothing new on either side, so I stay at 6.7.

401882300.overall: Mid-table neighbours one point apart: Córdoba (10th, 20 pts, 25 scored and 25 conceded) are unbeaten in five league games after a 3-3 at Mallorca, while Oviedo (9th, 21 pts) sacked Julián Calero last week and lost 1-2 at home to Girona in Raúl González's debut, with Santi Cazorla on his staff and a pressing, vertical style promised. The news the numbers do not know about is on Córdoba's side: Cristian Carracedo, their top assister (4), has a myofascial injury in his left leg, missed Mallorca and is not ruled out but is doubtful for Sunday (Cordópolis, El Debate); Kevin Medina is back in group training. Oviedo still miss Dani Calvo and Chris Ramos, which the numbers already count, and Oviedo have been far better away (13 of 21 points) than at home. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already adding both sides' scoring form (+3% and +1% momentum) and taking off Calvo and Ramos for Oviedo. I trim a little because Carracedo, Córdoba's top assister and a first-choice winger, is doubtful with a muscle injury the numbers do not list; Diego Bri and El Jebari covered well at Mallorca, so only a small cut: about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners, already up because Córdoba won 48 corners in their last six (+12% momentum). Carracedo's likely absence removes one wide outlet, but Córdoba kept attacking the flanks without him at Mallorca and Oviedo's new coach wants a direct, vertical team, so I stay at 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards; both teams are among the more booked in the division (Córdoba 48 yellows, Oviedo 45) and both are booking more lately, which momentum already adds (+10% and +9%). Carracedo is one yellow from a ban if he plays, and no referee has been named, so nothing new to size: I stay at 6.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, already raised by both teams' high recent shot counts (+12% and +13%). Raúl González wants Oviedo to press and play vertically, which fits an open game, while Carracedo's likely absence takes a little from Córdoba; these roughly balance, so I stay at 31.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target, already lifted by recent form on both sides. With Carracedo, Córdoba's main creator, doubtful and not in the numbers' absence list, I shade Córdoba's accuracy down slightly: about 10.2.

401882298.overall: Sporting (8th, 23 pts, only 16 goals scored) host Las Palmas (11th, 20 pts), who won four in a row before losing 1-0 at Granada; Las Palmas have not lost to Sporting in the last six meetings. Las Palmas miss Opoku (one-match ban, counted) and forward Sandro Ramírez (calf micro-tear, not in the numbers), but get Pezzolesi and Herzog back from the U21s. No referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take a lot off Sporting for Otero, Corredera, Sarco and Casas. Net a small cut to about 2.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with both sides' recent corner counts close to normal (+2% and +1% momentum). Sporting lose wide players Konrad and Pablo García, but Las Palmas' full-backs Pezzolesi and Andrés Rodríguez return to a settled back four that pushes on; nothing clearly shifts the count, so I stay at 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and already add both teams' heavy recent booking (+9% Sporting, +13% Las Palmas); Sporting have had two reds in two games (Otero's confrontation with the referee, Corredera's double yellow) and Opoku was sent off after 104 seconds at Granada. That trend is what momentum captures and no referee is named, so I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots, boosted by Sporting's high recent shot count (+12%). With Gelabert, Konrad and Pablo García out on top of the listed absences, Sporting's attack relies on young Enol Prendes and a thin front line, so I trim slightly to about 24.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target. Sporting are missing their most creative midfielder Gelabert (not in the numbers) and Las Palmas lose forward Sandro Ramírez for two to three weeks, so I shade down slightly to about 8.1.

401883109.overall: A top-five meeting: Girona (4th) and Eibar (5th) are level on 24 points, Eibar with a game in hand but no win in their last five league games (latest 1-1 at home to Cádiz). Quique Álvarez's Girona won 2-1 at Oviedo last week without Vanat (joint top scorer, 5 goals) and Holmes, who were on international duty and should be back. Girona miss Álex Moreno (fifth yellow, confirmed by the RFEF), Bryan Gil, Jastin García and Furtado, all already in the numbers; Eibar have no listed absences and have rotated heavily (only 31% of their XI kept over six games). Team news for this match was thin: club and league match pages had no preview text yet and no referee is named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and already count Moreno's ban (Girona lose a regular defender, which adds a little to Eibar) and the injured Girona attackers. Vanat's return after missing one game on international duty is normal availability that the base already assumes, and Eibar have scored just 7 in their last six; I stay at 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, with Girona's dominance expected (5.8 of them) and Eibar's habit of conceding many corners lately already added (+5% momentum). Without Álex Moreno, Girona lose their attacking left-back, but that is a small change, so I stay at 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.4 cards. Eibar are among the least booked sides (25 yellows in 13) and Girona have 35; Girona's most booked player, Moreno (5 yellows), is the one suspended. It is a tight play-off race game but no derby, and no referee is named, so I stay at 5.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with Girona's possession game expected to produce most of them (18.2) and Eibar's recent volume already added (+3%). Girona managed 21 shots at home to Celta Fortuna and dominated the ball at Oviedo; nothing new changes the picture, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, already adding Eibar's recent accuracy (+5%) and Girona's chance creation against a leaky Eibar defence lately (+8%). With no new injuries found on either side, I stay at 9.1.

401883304.overall: Celta Fortuna (17th, 13 pts, 26 conceded, no win in their last five) host Valladolid (12th, 18 pts) at Balaídos; Fredi Álvarez's reserve side sit just above the relegation places and usually play reactively (32% possession in a 5-1 loss at Girona). Valladolid miss Thiago Ojeda (fifth yellow, confirmed by the RFEF), Latasa and Guille Bueno; Celta Fortuna miss Gavián (injured in the 2-2 with Córdoba) and Sarppong; all of these are in the numbers. goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, already taking off Latasa (Valladolid's 10% of goal involvement) and Sarppong, and adding Valladolid's hot scoring run (14 in six). Celta Fortuna's leaky defence (26 conceded) and Álvaro Marín's 8 goals are in their record, and I found no new absences, so I stay at 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.2 corners and already add Valladolid's recent corner surge (+11% momentum), with Celta Fortuna winning few (17 in six). Celta's reserve side tends to sit deep and clear the ball, which is what those figures show, so I stay at 9.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.5 cards: both teams are among the most booked in the division and Celta Fortuna's recent booking rate is already added (+8%). Valladolid lose Ojeda to a fifth yellow, and the referee is not named yet, so there is nothing the numbers can't see: I stay at 6.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots, already lifted by Valladolid's high recent volume (+13%) and Celta Fortuna conceding many shots (99 in six). Without Latasa, Valladolid lean on Arnu (5 goals) and Ponceau's creativity, which the numbers partly account for; I stay at 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.9 shots on target, already up for Valladolid's sharp recent finishing (+15% momentum). I found no lineup news to change either side's attack, so I stay at 9.9.

401876395.overall: A relegation six-pointer: Troyes are 17th with 8 points, Le Havre last with 2 and the only Ligue 1 side without a win after six straight defeats, six points from safety. Le Havre replaced Didier Digard with Valérien Ismaël (contract to the end of the season, announced 12 November); with the international break he has had about a week of training, and this is his first game in charge and his first ever in France. Troyes (Stéphane Dumont) have tightened up, with two clean sheets in their last three league games, but they create the fewest big chances in the league. The league's discipline committee confirmed on 4 November that Troyes defender Junior Diaz serves a one-match ban for yellow cards from 10 November, so he misses this game (the numbers count it; some previews still name him in the lineup); Troyes also miss Ouzenadji and forward Yacouba Koné is doubtful with a knee problem. Le Havre are without Mpasi, Mambimbi and Zagadou, with Pembélé, Jelert and midfielder Rassoul Ndiaye doubtful; referee Jérémie Pignard (4.4 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, and they already count Diaz's ban for Troyes (+6% for Le Havre) and Ouzenadji's absence (-4.5% for Troyes). I keep a small lean lower (-4%), to about 2.2: Troyes create the fewest big chances in the league and have kept two clean sheets in three, and a new coach after a week of training usually starts by tightening up. Previews expect a low score (Sports Mole 0-1, another 1-1).

corners.text: The numbers say 8.7 corners, with Troyes the bigger share at home (5.2); recent corner form on both sides is in the numbers. Previews disagree on how Ismaël will line Le Havre up (a back three or a back four), so there is no clear sign of a change in how they attack. I stay at about 8.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, and they already add 17% for referee Jérémie Pignard (4.4 cards a game in 44 matches). I keep a small lean higher (+5%), to about 5.0: it is a bottom-two six-pointer, a defeat would leave Le Havre adrift under a coach brought in as an emergency fix, and both sides should play with extra edge, which the numbers' season-long view does not see.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.8 shots. Le Havre have been shooting a lot lately (107 in their last six) while losing every game, and Troyes create little; the numbers already count that recent form. A new coach could make Le Havre either bolder or more careful, and nothing yet points one way, so I stay at about 24.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.7 shots on target. I lean slightly lower (-3%), to about 7.5, in line with goals: Troyes are last in the league for big chances and a tense game between the bottom two with a new coach bedding in should produce few clear shots. Missing players on both sides (Diaz, Ouzenadji, Le Havre's injured defenders) are already counted.

401876398.overall: Leaders PSG (23 points, five straight league wins) visit sixth-placed Nice, who have won three league games in a row under Olivier Pantaloni and whose sporting director talks about a disciplined, compact display. The numbers take goals off PSG for Dembélé, Marquinhos, Akliouche and Kvaratskhelia, but Le Parisien (via Maxifoot, 18 Nov) says the staff are optimistic Dembélé, Marquinhos, Nuno Mendes and Akliouche can all return, with Luis Enrique waiting on training before deciding; Kvaratskhelia stays out, and Doué still appears on Foot Mercato's injury list. PSG host Roma in the Champions League on Wednesday, so returning players will likely get limited minutes. Foot Mercato's list also shows Nice without Abdelmonem, Clauss, Sanson, Boudaoui and Diop, none of whom the numbers count, though I could not confirm each one elsewhere. Referee Jérôme Brisard (4.2 cards a game) is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals after taking about 20% off PSG's goals for Dembélé, Marquinhos and Akliouche (plus Kvaratskhelia, who really is out). I lean higher (+5%), to about 2.9: reports say those three plus Nuno Mendes should be back, though with managed minutes before Roma, and Nice may be missing several players the numbers don't count (Abdelmonem, Clauss, Sanson, Boudaoui on one injury list). Doué's doubt keeps the size small.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, with PSG taking the larger share (5.2). Nice plan to defend compactly and break, which usually hands PSG corners, but the numbers already see PSG's dominance and Nice without Clauss lose some crossing from the right. These pull in opposite directions, so I stay at about 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, already adding about 10% for Jérôme Brisard (4.2 a game), plus Nice's recent rise in bookings (18 in six) and PSG's very low count (4 in six). A Nice side chasing the ball against PSG may foul more, but that pattern is what the numbers already describe, so I stay at about 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.7 shots, with PSG's recent high volume already in them. I lean slightly higher (+2%), to about 30.3: Dembélé and Akliouche returning adds shooting, and Nice possibly missing midfielders Sanson and Boudaoui could leave them under more pressure. Kept small because the returners' minutes will be managed before the Roma game.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 12.3 shots on target, already up 20% for PSG's sharp recent form (60 on target in six). I lean a little higher (+3%), to about 12.7: the numbers treat Dembélé and Akliouche as out, but both are expected back in the squad, and Nice's defence may be weakened by absences the numbers don't count. Doué's doubt and the coming Roma game keep it small.

401876399.overall: Monaco (7th, 16 points) are without a league win in five under Filipe Luis; their last game was a 1-1 at Le Mans with a 90th-minute equaliser, although they have won both recent Conference League games. Auxerre (14th, 10 points) under Will Still have lost two in a row, including 5-1 at Strasbourg, and leak goals away from home; Clément Archer (6 goals) is their main threat. Idumbo and Ansu Fati for Monaco and Okoh, Dioussé and Fofana for Auxerre are already counted; Foot Mercato's injury list also shows Golovin (and others with no clear status) for Monaco, and an earlier report said Golovin was doubtful, while Auxerre's Labeau-Lascary and Akpa also appear on it. Referee Jérémy Stinat (confirmed by Auxerre, 4.1 cards a game) is already counted. News was thin: no written preview of this match was out yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, with Monaco expected to score about 2.0 against an Auxerre side that conceded 5 at Strasbourg and 4 at Rennes. I lean slightly lower (-3%), to about 3.0: Golovin, Monaco's main creator, is listed as injured and not counted by the numbers, and Monaco have scored only eight in their last six league games while Brunner's early burst has cooled. Idumbo's absence is already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, most of them Monaco's (5.7) as the side expected to have the ball. Auxerre usually sit back away from home, which the numbers already reflect; Golovin missing would cut some set-piece delivery but not obviously the number of corners. I stay at about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.5 cards, already adding 7.5% for Jérémy Stinat (4.1 cards a game in 39 matches). There is no derby or special edge here: Monaco need a win to end their run and Auxerre will defend, which is a normal pattern the numbers capture. I stay at about 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 23.9 shots, with Monaco about 14.6. Auxerre's shot output has dropped lately (62 in six, counted by the numbers), and Monaco's lack of wins comes more from finishing than volume. Golovin's absence could trim Monaco's shots a little, but not enough to move it, so I stay at about 23.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. I lean slightly lower (-2%), to about 9.1: without Golovin, who creates most of Monaco's best chances, their shot quality is likely a bit lower than the numbers assume. Auxerre's absences (Okoh, Dioussé, Fofana) are already counted.

401876403.overall: Two sides level on 13 points, but Lens are in turmoil: after a 9-1 Champions League defeat at Como, coach Yannick Cahuzac was dismissed, a return of Pierre Sage collapsed, and Didier Digard was named coach on 13 November (until 2028), so this is his first game after about a week of training over the international break. Lens have lost their last two league games and conceded 17 in their last six in all competitions; Digard's record is building organised, hard-to-beat sides. Édouard, Ganiou, Sima, Nawrocki and Chávez are out and already counted, while defender Gradit is back training fully and Ivanović should be over his concussion. Toulouse (Jens Berthel Askou) create chances but finish poorly, with Tengstedt (5) their top scorer; Messali's absence is counted. Referee Bastien Dechepy (4.4 cards a game) is already counted. No written preview of this match was out yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, and their momentum boost for Toulouse (+5%) leans on Lens conceding 17 in six, nine of them in one freak night at Como. I lean lower (-5%), to about 2.6: Digard's first priority will be a tighter defence, and his teams have been organised, while Toulouse have missed a lot of big chances. Lens' missing forwards (Édouard, Sima, Ganiou) are already counted.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners, with Lens at home taking the bigger share (5.5) despite fewer corners lately (26 in six, counted). Under Cahuzac Lens played with wing-backs who drive corners, and nothing yet says Digard will change the shape in his first week. I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.9 cards, already including +15.5% for Bastien Dechepy (4.4 cards a game) and a small boost from past meetings. A new coach's first home game can bring extra intensity, but that is a hunch rather than news, and neither side has a disciplinary trend the numbers miss, so I stay at about 4.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.0 shots, with Lens' recent dip in shooting (70 in six against 85 expected) already taking about 5% off. A more cautious first game under Digard might lower Lens' volume, but a home crowd demanding a reaction pulls the other way, so I stay at about 25.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, already lifting Toulouse for a Lens defence that let in 35 on target in six, a run skewed by the Como game. I lean slightly lower (-3%), to about 8.5, in line with goals: a new coach should first make Lens harder to open up, and Toulouse's finishing has been poor.

401876402.overall: Second-placed Lille (21 pts) host fifth-placed Lyon (17 pts), who arrive after a 2-0 defeat at Brest and with a new coach: Paulo Fonseca left for Sporting and Carlos Vicens, a former Guardiola assistant, was appointed on 9 November, so this is his first game on the bench (Olympique & Lyonnais, Get French Football News, Foot01). Lyon are without Morton, Sulc (knee surgery, out until February or March), Ouedraogo and Openda (foot surgery), all already in the numbers; Lille miss Tiago Santos (ACL) and Igamane, while striker Ayase Ueda is only doubtful after a month out with a foot injury (the numbers count him out). Lille host Bayern in the Champions League four days later and refused a Sunday date to protect that game, and Lyon fans are banned from travelling by the prefecture because of nationwide protests. François Letexier referees (4.0 cards per game, already counted); he sent off Lyon's Nakamura earlier this season.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals and already take off for Lyon's missing scorers Sulc and Openda and for Lille's Ueda and Tiago Santos. Ueda is listed as doubtful rather than out, but he has barely trained for a month, so at most he is a bench option; a new Lyon coach in his first game could go either way. Lille have one of the best defences in the league (five clean sheets by early November), which fits a low number, so I stay at about 2.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, with Lille's recent dip in corners (25 in six games) already in them. Vicens comes from the Guardiola school and is expected to want more possession than Fonseca's side, but after only a week of training (and internationals returning late) I can't size a change in Lyon's play yet. I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards, including Letexier's slightly above-average record (+5% already counted) and Lyon's quieter card run lately. A second-versus-fifth game has edge, but there will be no away fans in the stadium and a new coach's first match is not usually a heated one; these pull in opposite directions, so I stay at about 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 21.9 shots, already trimmed for both sides' quieter recent shooting. Lille may manage minutes with Bayern coming on Wednesday, but the club fought to keep the game on Saturday, so a strong side is likely; Lyon's attack is thin without Openda and Sulc, which the numbers know. I stay at about 21.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target and already cut Lyon's for their recent form (22 on target in six games) and missing attackers. Nothing new on either side points to sharper or blunter finishing than that, so I stay at about 8.3.

401876396.overall: Strasbourg (13th, 10 pts, LLLWL) host Brest (9th, 15 pts), who have won at Lorient and beaten Lyon 2-0 without conceding. Strasbourg's coach Hugo Oliveira is under heavy pressure: Maxifoot (citing L'Equipe) reported on 17 November that a deal with Swansea's Vitor Matos was close, and Foot01 (citing The Athletic) calls a change imminent, but Brest's own preview on 18 November still names Oliveira, so who is on the bench is unclear. Strasbourg have the fourth-best attack but the 16th defence (22 conceded); Panichelli (ACL), Oyedele and Fabio Baldé are out and already counted. The game marks the club's 120th anniversary with about 200 former players at the Meinau. Azzedine Souifi referees his first Brest game; the numbers know only four of his top-flight games.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already well above a usual Ligue 1 game because of Strasbourg's open games at both ends. I lean slightly lower, to about 3.2: Brest have just kept two clean sheets and win games on the break, and a side in coaching limbo (or a new coach's first game) tends to start cautiously. An earlier report had Giovanni Reyna (3 goals) out with a thigh problem; I could not confirm it, so it carries little weight.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners and already know both sides have won few corners lately (Strasbourg 16, Brest 15 in their last six). Brest are happy without the ball and Strasbourg's attack runs through quick forwards like Harder and Godo rather than wide crossing; nothing new changes that, so I stay at about 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, using Souifi's small top-flight sample (3.5 cards in 4 games, blended with an average referee). Brest's preview gives his wider record as about 4 yellows and 0.3 reds per game, a bit stricter than the numbers assume, and a tense home crowd on an anniversary night with the coach's job at stake adds a little; I go to about 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.9 shots, with Strasbourg's recent volume (73 in six) and Brest's slightly lower output already in them. Strasbourg will push in front of their own crowd and Brest sit and counter, which is how the numbers already see it, so I stay at about 24.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. I trim slightly to about 8.6 for the same reasons as goals: Brest's tight recent defending (16 on target conceded in six) and a cautious start likely from a Strasbourg side unsure of its coach.

401876397.overall: Third-placed Paris FC (20 pts) host Angers (16th, 8 pts, one point from their last five). Liam Rosenior's side are unbeaten at Jean-Bouin and rely heavily on Lassine Sinayoko, the league's top scorer with nine goals, who scored the winner at Auxerre; Ikoné and Sangui are out and already counted. Angers (Stéphane Gilli) have conceded heavily lately (beaten 2-0 by Lyon and Nice), have used a five-man defence away from home, and miss the suspended Lefort and Bané Diatta. The numbers cut Angers' attack by about a fifth for striker Amine El Ouazzani; the previous view cited an Ouest-France report that he is back, which I could not open to re-check. Aurélien Petit referees (2.5 cards per game in four games, already counted).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, with Angers' attack cut by about 19% for El Ouazzani. The previous view cited an Ouest-France report on 17 November that he is back; I could not re-check it and he may lack sharpness, so I give back only a small part, to about 2.6. Paris FC's home attack around Sinayoko and Pagis is already fully in the numbers.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Paris FC should have most of the ball against an Angers side that has dropped into a back five away from home, which the numbers already reflect in their home-heavy split (5.1 v 3.7); nothing new changes it, so I stay at about 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already lowered for Aurélien Petit's lenient start (2.5 per game) and raised a little for Angers' recent card count. Angers lose Lefort to suspension, which the numbers know; a one-sided game against a struggling side usually brings fouls from the away team but not a heated match, so I stay at about 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots, already pushed up for Paris FC's busy recent shooting (86 in six) and for Angers conceding a lot (106 shots in six). That matches what the reports describe (Angers 'suffered a lot' at Lyon), so I stay at about 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. With El Ouazzani possibly back (one report, not re-checked) Angers have a bit more threat than the numbers assume, so I go slightly up, to about 9.0.

401876401.overall: A Breton derby between Lorient (10th, 15 pts) and Rennes (8th, 16 pts), one point apart. Rennes have won one of their last six in all competitions, conceded 21 league goals, and their chairman put Franck Haise under public pressure on 17 November, with Blas, Nordin and Merlin reportedly pushed out of the squad (Maxifoot, Foot01, GFFN). The numbers count Rennes' top scorer Esteban Lepaul (7 goals in 7 games, ankle sprain) as out; he was close to a return before the break and an earlier report said he is set to play here, but I could not re-confirm it. Lorient (Alexandre Dujeux) are a stubborn defensive side who won 2-0 at Le Havre last time; Katseris, Fadiga, Bamba and Ibrahima Baldé are in the numbers' missing list. Marc Bollengier referees (4.1 cards per game, already counted); no match preview was out yet, so the view leans on club and league news.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and cut Rennes' by about 20% for Lepaul. Sports Mole said on 8 November he might return soon and after the two-week break a comeback is plausible (one earlier report said he is set to play), so I give back part of that, to about 2.6. Lorient's tight defence (four conceded in six) is already counted and keeps this modest.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners, with Rennes slightly ahead (5.1 v 4.3). Haise has switched between a back three with wing-backs and a 4-3-3, and Lorient sit deep at home, which the numbers already reflect; I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, including Bollengier's slightly strict record (+6% already counted). A derby between neighbours with Rennes under pressure has some edge, but the brief carries no derby flag and both sides' recent card counts are normal, so I stay at about 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.9 shots, already up for Rennes' busy shooting (85 in six) and down for Lorient's low volume. A Lepaul return would change who finishes the chances more than how many Rennes create, so I stay at about 25.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. Lepaul, if he plays, is Rennes' most accurate finisher, so I go slightly up to about 9.3; Lorient's low recent output on target (14 in six) is already in the numbers.

401882805.overall: Athletic (7th, 16 pts) host Espanyol (13th, 12 pts) on Friday night at San Mamés, the first game after the international break; Athletic have climbed out of trouble under Edin Terzic, and only Sevilla have won at San Mamés this season. Vivian (soleus, back in about two weeks), Guruzeta and Sannadi are out, but Terzic said on Thursday that Aitor Paredes is available after all, while the numbers still take him off; local press expect Yeray or Paredes, possibly the young Iker Monreal, next to or instead of Laporte, and Yeray, Berenguer and Yuri only trained apart to manage their load. Espanyol play their second game under Eder Sarabia, who wants a possession side and switches between three and four at the back; Edu Expósito has shaken off his knock and is expected to be available, Kike García and Calatrava (torn ACL) are out and Urko is a doubt. Mateo Busquets Ferrer referees (VAR Iglesias Villanueva); the numbers already count his high card record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals and take about 8% off Athletic's scoring because they think Aitor Paredes is out, but Terzic said on Thursday he is available (he may start or come off the bench). Edu Expósito, Espanyol's main creator, is also expected to be fit after a week of doubt, while Athletic's back line without Vivian is less settled. That gives back part of the cut, so a mild nudge up to about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, 6.4 of them Athletic's, and already add Athletic's recent corners against an Espanyol side that conceded 44 in six games. Nico Williams is fit and back from Spain duty, so Athletic's usual wide game at San Mamés stays. Sarabia wants Espanyol to keep the ball more, but one game (a 0-0 with Deportivo) is too little to say they will concede fewer corners, so I keep 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers now say 6.6 cards: they add about 29% for referee Mateo Busquets Ferrer (around 5.8 cards a game on their record; 5.3 yellows and 0.3 reds a game over four seasons in one count) and about 9% for Espanyol's heavy card run (20 in six), nearly all of it under Manolo González's deep, combative side. Sarabia's team is built to keep the ball and press higher, which usually means fewer fouls from chasing the game, and his debut was a calm 0-0. The referee is already counted, so I only keep the mild trim for the change of style, to about 6.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.1 shots, with Athletic taking 17.7, and already add Athletic's busy recent shooting (94 in six games). Athletic are short of a central striker with Guruzeta and Sannadi out, but Iñaki and Nico Williams and Sancet carry most of the shooting and Terzic said everyone else is available. Espanyol's new possession plan could cut Athletic's share a little, but there is not enough evidence yet, so I keep 26.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target and already take a bit off Espanyol for their weak recent finishing (18 on target in six). Edu Expósito being fit helps Espanyol a little, but Kike García is still out and Puado is not expected to last 90 minutes, while Athletic's attack is close to full strength. Nothing the numbers miss clearly moves it, so 8.4.

401882806.overall: Alavés (12th, 13 pts) host Deportivo (9th, 15 pts) at Mendizorroza on Saturday lunchtime in what Alavés call a game against a direct rival. Quique Sánchez Flores' side have gone eight league games without a win, scoring only five goals in that run, and set up in a cautious 5-3-2 (last time out a 0-0 at Sevilla with two shots on target); Toni Martínez has not scored all season. Alavés miss Mikel Rodríguez (in the numbers), plus Garcés and Diarra long-term. Antonio Hidalgo's Deportivo get Aubameyang back after injury (involved in seven of their fifteen goals; he came off the bench in recent games and is in the probable XI) and Casadó is regaining rhythm, while Bright Ede and Eddahchouri are doubts and Mella and Giménez return late from international duty. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already cut Alavés a little for their poor scoring run and for Mikel Rodríguez. What they don't see is Aubameyang back for Deportivo: he was out for a spell, is involved in seven of their fifteen goals and is in the probable XI. Alavés' defensive 5-3-2 holds me to a mild nudge, to about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners and already take some off Alavés for their low recent count (19 in six games) and add Deportivo's busy run (41). Quique's side defend deep and attack mostly through Boyé and long balls, which the momentum already reflects. Nothing new changes either side's approach, so I keep 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards and already take a little off for both sides' quiet recent card counts (Alavés 10 and Deportivo 12 in six games). It is a tense game near the bottom half, but neither side has a discipline issue in the news, Amatucci is one booking from a ban, and no referee is named yet. I stay at 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots and already add about 16% to Deportivo for their heavy recent shooting (96 in six games). Aubameyang's return adds more box threat than extra volume, and Alavés' low shot count fits their cautious set-up, which the numbers already count. I keep 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. Aubameyang starting gives Deportivo a finisher who gets more of their attempts on target than the forwards who played while he was out. Alavés themselves managed only two on target at Sevilla, so the nudge is small, to about 8.7.

401882799.overall: Rayo (14th, 12 pts) host Valencia (19th, 9 pts, only 8 goals scored) at Vallecas on Saturday, a game Javier Aguirre's Valencia badly need. The numbers take Umar Sadiq out for Valencia, but three reports (16-18 Nov) say he has recovered from a knee knock, trained normally and is expected to start. Valencia still miss Gayà (banned, red card against Real Madrid), Jesús Vázquez, Otorbi and Diego López, and Danjuma is doubtful after medical tests on a thigh problem; Maffeo and Guido Rodríguez are one booking from a ban. Beñat San José's Rayo are without Álvaro García, Batalla and Luiz Felipe (all in the numbers), with Óscar Valentín and Kumbulla doubtful. No referee has been named.

goals.text: The numbers say 1.9 goals, after cutting Valencia's scoring by about 16% for Umar Sadiq being out. Elgoldigital, Eldesmarque and FutbolFantasy all report he has trained normally after his knee knock and should start, so I add back part of that: about 2.0 goals. Not all of it, because Danjuma (already taken off by the numbers) is still doubtful and Valencia rarely score anyway.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners and already add some for Valencia conceding plenty lately (39 in six games). Sadiq is a target man rather than a winger, so his return changes little for corners, and Rayo's wide play through De Frutos and Ratiu is already in their usual numbers. I keep 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards and already add about 12% for Valencia's heavy recent card count (19 in six games). Valencia are desperate and Vallecas is a tight, noisy ground, but Maffeo and Guido Rodríguez, one booking from a ban, may hold back a little; no referee is named. Those balance out, so 5.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.0 shots and already add about 22% to Rayo for their heavy shooting against a Valencia side that concedes a lot of attempts. With Sadiq up front Valencia have a focal point who wins duels and gets shots off, rather than the thin attack the numbers assumed, so I nudge it up to about 29.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.4 shots on target and take some off for Valencia's attack without Sadiq. His likely start gives Valencia more chances to test Audero than the numbers assume, so I move it to about 8.7. Rayo's own on-target count is already raised by their recent form.

401882797.overall: The Seville derby: Luis García Plaza's Sevilla (6th, 18 pts) host Manuel Pellegrini's in-form Betis (4th, 26 pts) at the Pizjuán on Saturday evening; Betis play Slovan Bratislava in Europe three days later, but the derby comes first. Betis still have Cucho Hernández (in the numbers as out) working only partly with the group after a soleus injury, so he is at best a bench option, and Dani Ceballos became a doubt on Tuesday with thigh discomfort, which the numbers do not know. Facundo Bernal, listed as banned, has served his four-game suspension and is available again. Sevilla are without Carmona, Sierra and Alfon González, Rubén Vargas left Switzerland's camp with discomfort and is a doubt, while Isaac Romero, Fofana and Peque are back in training. No referee has been named; the numbers already add a large derby boost to cards.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and take off about 10% of Betis' scoring for Cucho Hernández and some of Sevilla's for Sierra. Cucho is back in partial training and could make the bench, but Ceballos, involved in both goals against Elche, is now a doubt, and Sevilla may lose Vargas. Those pull both ways, so I stay at 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.0 corners and already take some off Sevilla for their low recent count (19 in six games). Vargas, used mainly for set pieces, is doubtful, but Félix Correia would take the left wing, so Sevilla's approach should not change much. I keep 9.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 7.0 cards, already including a large derby boost (about +39%). Bernal, an aggressive holding midfielder, is available again after his ban, but Marc Roca has held the spot and may keep it, and no referee is named yet. With the derby already counted in full, I don't add more and stay at 7.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.4 shots and already add Betis' busy recent shooting (97 in six games). Isaac Romero and Fofana, who trained in the gym last week, look set to play for Sevilla, and Betis' many internationals got back only midweek. Nothing clear moves it, so 27.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.2 shots on target and already add Betis' good recent finishing. Ceballos' doubt and Cucho's limited fitness could take a little off Betis, Vargas' doubt a little off Sevilla, but none of it is confirmed. I stay at 9.2.

401882798.overall: Real Madrid (2nd, 30 pts, an eight-match winning run in all competitions) host Celta (11th, one win in five) on Saturday night, three days before PSV visit the Bernabéu in the Champions League. Madrid are short at the back: Mendy (thigh) and Asencio (tibia surgery) are out, along with Rodrygo, and Tchouaméni (adductor) and Bernardo Silva are doubts; only Tchouaméni and Rodrygo are in the numbers' list. Mbappé, who has scored in seven straight games, missed France v Italy with a minor knock but stayed with the squad, so he looks available. Celta are worse hit than the numbers know: Borja Iglesias and Miguel Román are ruled out, and defenders Starfelt and Álvaro Núñez are still only training on their own. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals and already take off Moriba for Celta and Tchouaméni for Madrid. Celta are also without midfielder Miguel Román, and likely without defenders Starfelt and Álvaro Núñez, none of whom the numbers count. Madrid's missing full-back Mendy and centre-back Asencio give Celta a little more of a chance too. A small lean up to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners, already trimmed for both sides' recent low corner counts. Madrid should pin a weakened Celta back, but they tend to go through the middle rather than win corners, and Mendy's absence takes away some overlapping down the left. Nothing clear enough to move it, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already lowered because both teams have picked up fewer cards than usual lately. No referee has been named, the game has no derby or table edge, and a Celta side likely to sit deep and chase the ball rarely builds a tense game at the Bernabéu. I keep 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.0 shots and already add Madrid's heavy recent shooting (108 in six games). A Celta side missing Miguel Román in midfield and possibly two defenders should give Madrid even more of the ball, though with PSV on Tuesday and many internationals only back on Thursday, some rotation is possible. A small lean up to about 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, with Madrid's recent accuracy already counted. Mbappé looks fit despite missing a France game with a minor knock, and Celta's back line is thinner than the numbers know (Starfelt and Álvaro Núñez still training alone). A small lean up to about 10.7.

401882804.overall: Leaders Barcelona (33 pts, 24-7 at home) host Villarreal (8th) at midday on Sunday, the first of seven Barça games in 21 days. Barça get Dani Olmo back in training (the numbers take him as out) and Koundé is expected back with the group on Thursday; Cubarsí (hip flexor overload, taken as out by the numbers) is a real doubt, and Rodri, Xavi Espart and Bardghji stay out. Villarreal under Iñigo Pérez have had a poor autumn, including a 6-0 loss at PSG, and miss Gerard Moreno, Akhomach and Foyth (all in the numbers) plus Diatta, out long-term with a hamstring injury, whom the numbers do not list. No referee yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already high, and they cut Barça's scoring for Olmo, who is back in training and expected to be available, and Villarreal's for Gerard Moreno and Akhomach. If Cubarsí plays, the numbers' boost for Villarreal (they took him as out) is too big, which pulls the other way. With Olmo back and Villarreal also missing Diatta, a slight lean up to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners and already add Villarreal's high recent corner count (41 in six). Barça will have most of the ball, and Lamine Yamal and Raphinha drive a lot of wide play, but nothing in the news changes either side's approach. I stay at 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.4 cards and already add Villarreal's busy recent card record (15 in six). No referee has been named and the match has no special edge; a side chasing the ball at Camp Nou often picks up tactical fouls, which the Villarreal numbers already reflect. I keep 4.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, with both sides' recent shooting already added. Olmo's return helps Barça's chance creation, but Flick is managing muscle overloads before a run of seven games in 21 days and may limit minutes. These roughly balance, so I stay at 28.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. Olmo and Koundé coming back makes Barça's attack closer to full strength than the numbers assume, and Villarreal have looked open lately (six conceded at PSG). A slight lean up to about 10.8.

401882800.overall: Racing (10th, 14 pts) host in-form Real Sociedad (5th, four wins in five) at El Sardinero on Sunday afternoon. Racing are a different side at home (11 of their 14 points, 1.5 goals conceded per game there against 3.5 away) and are expected to repeat the XI that won 2-1 at Málaga, with Zabiri (9 goals) in form; Mantilla (season) and Andrés Martín are out, as the numbers know. Real Sociedad miss Barrenetxea and Odriozola, Aihen Muñoz has discomfort and Mamadou Sarr is a serious doubt with a calf problem; there is some doubt over who starts in midfield and up front (Óskarsson or Sucic). One fantasy site marks Óskarsson as suspended without explanation, and a second preview does not, so I treat him as available. No referee named yet; both previews expect an open game with goals.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals and already take off Barrenetxea and Andrés Martín and add Real Sociedad's strong recent scoring. Racing have yet to keep a clean sheet, but they are much tighter at El Sardinero than away, and Real Sociedad's only new doubt (Sarr) is a centre-back. These pull both ways, so I stay at 3.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.3 corners, already trimmed for Real Sociedad's lower recent corner count. Racing play with wing-backs and Real Sociedad attack down the flanks with Guedes and Kubo, but nothing new changes that. I keep 11.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.2 cards and already add Racing's high recent card count (18 in six). Several players on both sides (Pablo Ramón, Zabiri, Aramburu, Yangel Herrera) are one yellow from a ban, which can make them a little more careful, but no referee has been named. I stay at 5.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots and already add both sides' busy recent shooting (94 and 96 in six). Previews expect two attacking teams to trade chances, which is what the numbers already show, so I keep 31.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target. Zabiri and Real Sociedad's Óskarsson are both scoring freely, but both are expected to be available, as the numbers assume. No change, 10.4.

401882801.overall: Osasuna (16th, 12 pts) host bottom side Málaga (5 pts, no wins in 12, no away clean sheet) on Sunday evening in a game both need badly. Budimir (8 goals) is back in training after Croatia duty; Bretones (soleus) and Aitor Fernández are out to mid-December and winger Del Castillo is a doubt with a slight adductor problem, which the numbers do not list. Málaga have Aznou banned and miss Lobete, Ochoa and Murillo (all in the numbers), while Rafita and Juan Cruz are doubts. Málaga lost 2-1 at home to Racing last time out. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already give Málaga a small boost for Bretones being out. Osasuna have scored only 12 in 12 and may be without Del Castillo, one of their main creators, which the numbers don't know, and previews expect a tight, nervy game between two struggling sides. A small lean down to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, with both sides' recent corner counts already counted. Osasuna lean on crosses for Budimir, which brings corners, but losing Del Castillo on the wing could reduce them a little; it balances out. I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards; they already add Osasuna's recent cards (19 in six) and take some off for Málaga's quieter run, and they make no adjustment for the stakes. A relegation six-pointer with a winless bottom side that must take risks tends to be scrappy; Málaga's Aznou is already banned for a second yellow. A small lean up to about 4.8; no referee named yet.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting and how much each concedes (+11% each). Del Castillo's doubt and a cautious game point a little lower, but that is already a large adjustment in the other direction, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target. Budimir is fit and back after the break, as the numbers assume, and Málaga's recent accuracy (33 on target in six) is already counted. No clear reason to move it, so 9.6.

401879233.overall: City are third but come out of the international break on a three-game league losing run (last 3-1 at Forest), so Enzo Maresca has every reason to field a strong side at home, although one preview tags City as heavy rotators (45% of the XI kept over six games) with a Champions League game three days later. Fulham sit 15th under Alvaro Arbeloa and are four league games unbeaten (LWWDD); one report says Tom Cairney misses out with a knee problem. On City's side Semenyo is out until December and Guéhi (hip/groin, rated 75% to play) and Gvardiol (taken off at half-time at Forest) are doubts, with Khusanov also carrying a knock; the numbers already treat Semenyo and Guéhi as out. Referee Thomas Bramall averages slightly fewer cards than the league (counted). Overall the news pulls both ways and I stay with the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already take off Semenyo (about -10% on City's goals) and Guéhi. If Guéhi plays (75% per the FPL flag) City concede a little less than assumed, but Gvardiol is a new doubt at the back, so the defensive picture roughly nets out; City's recent leaks and Fulham's unbeaten run are in the momentum figures. So I stay at about 2.8.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.2 corners. City should dominate the ball at home after three defeats, with Doku and Cherki wide, while Fulham defend in a 4-5-1 and rely on Robinson and Castagne's overlaps; that is the usual shape of this fixture and the numbers already reflect it, so I stay at about 10.2.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. Referee Thomas Bramall (3.8 per game, below the 4.0 average) and Fulham's recent run of bookings are both already counted, and nothing points to extra edge: Fulham have no suspensions pending and the stakes are ordinary. So about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.8 shots. One preview expects City to rotate before midweek Europe and City have Gvardiol and Khusanov doubts, which would trim their output, but after three straight defeats and a fresh squad out of the break Maresca is more likely to push hard at home; the two pull in opposite directions, so I keep about 25.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, with Semenyo's absence (City's second scorer behind Haaland) already counted. Haaland and Cherki are expected to start and Fulham report no new absences up front, so with rotation risk and City's reaction to their losing run cancelling out I stay at about 8.8.

401879238.overall: Bournemouth are seventh and flying: six straight wins in all competitions, with Evanilson scoring in each of his last five league games, though they rotate heavily (35% of the XI kept over six games). Forest are 16th under Oliver Glasner but beat Manchester City 3-1 last time out. Bournemouth's absences (Juanlu Sánchez, Araujo, Tóth) and Forest's (Savona, Domínguez) are already in the numbers; new for Forest are doubts over Neco Williams (hurt with Wales, ankle, 75%), Xaver Schlager (thigh, back from Austria for treatment) and Dan Ndoye (left Switzerland early for workload).
