Referee Adam Herczeg has few Premier League games on record and is counted. The Forest doubts are the one thing the numbers can't see, so I trim Forest's output slightly.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, already counting Bournemouth's hot scoring run and Forest's thin attack (5 goals in six). Neco Williams has started all ten league games and is a key outlet from wing-back, and Schlager and Ndoye are also doubts; none of that is in the numbers, so I trim a little to about 2.65.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Bournemouth press high and attack the flanks through Kluivert and Tavernier, while Forest's 3-4-2-1 leans on Muñoz and Williams wide; if Williams misses out Ola Aina is a like-for-like swap, so the shape barely changes and I stay at about 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, already including Forest's recent rise in bookings and referee Adam Herczeg (only two games on record, so mostly the league average). Forest are near the bottom and will compete physically, but nothing beyond what is counted points to a more heated game, so about 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots. Forest have kept a settled XI (85%) and possible absences of Williams, Schlager and Ndoye would weaken their supply line more than the numbers know, while Bournemouth's heavy rotation is a habit their figures already carry; so a small trim to about 25.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already marking Forest down for their poor recent accuracy (-10% momentum). The same Forest doubts take a touch more off their side, so about 8.0.

401878756.overall: Villa are tenth and unbeaten in five under Unai Emery, but they travel to Galatasaray in the Champions League on Tuesday 24 November, so some rotation is expected (51% of the XI kept over six games). Onana and Ruggeri are out and Cash (concussion protocol), Wan-Bissaka and Manzambi are doubts. Sunderland are 19th under Régis Le Bris, who is under pressure despite the 1-0 win over Chelsea before the break; Brobbey (small upper-leg tear, out a few weeks per one Dutch report) and Xhaka (calf) are counted as out by the numbers, as are Ballard, Diarra and Mundle. One tracker lists Hume and Danso as suspended, but Danso's one-game ban was served against Leeds on 25 October and no other outlet reports a ban, so I treat both as available. Referee Andy Madley shows fewer cards than average (counted).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals and already take a big chunk off Sunderland for losing Brobbey (about -23% on their goals). What they can't see is Villa rotating with a trip to Istanbul on Tuesday and Cash, Wan-Bissaka and Manzambi all doubtful, which trims the home side's output a little, so about 2.5.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Villa will have most of the ball and Sunderland, who rotate heavily themselves (25% of the XI kept), tend to sit in and break; rotation changes the names more than the shape, so I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards, already counting referee Andy Madley (3.7 a game) and Sunderland's recent bookings. The reported Sunderland suspensions look out of date (Danso served his ban in October), so there is nothing new on discipline; about 4.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.1 shots, pushed up by both sides' recent shot volume. Emery usually freshens the side before a Champions League away trip and a rotated Villa usually shoots a bit less, while Sunderland have no recognised top scorer fit without Brobbey; so about 27.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.5 shots on target. The same expected Villa rotation before Galatasaray trims it a little, to about 8.2; Sunderland's weaker attack without Brobbey and Xhaka is already in the numbers.

401879236.overall: A close one on paper: Chelsea fifth under Xabi Alonso after losing at Sunderland before the break, Leeds ninth under Daniel Farke after a 1-0 win over Tottenham and with a settled XI (same eleven three games running). Chelsea are without Reece James and Lacroix, with João Pedro (thigh, 'slight chance'), Hato and Jamie Gittens (ankle, hurt with England Under-21s) major doubts and Caicedo a minor doubt after Ecuador duty; the numbers already count João Pedro, Lacroix and Hato as out but not Gittens. Leeds have only Mateo Joseph out (counted), with Stach (foot, about 50%) and Gudmundsson (expected back in training) doubts. Michael Oliver referees, at exactly the league average for cards (counted).

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and already remove João Pedro (about -19% on Chelsea's goals). Gittens, another forward, is a major doubt the numbers don't know about, and Caicedo's knock could weaken Chelsea's control; a small chance João Pedro plays pulls the other way, so only a slight trim, to about 2.45.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Chelsea's wing-backs and Palmer drive most of their corners, and Leeds' 3-4-3 with wing-backs is settled; without Gittens Chelsea lose a dribbler but keep the same width, so I stay at about 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.7 cards, already counting Michael Oliver (4.0 a game over 84 games) and Leeds' recent rise in bookings. Farke wants to avenge the 6-3 Carabao Cup loss to Chelsea in September, but that is ordinary motivation and neither side has suspensions; about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.4 shots. Chelsea's thinner forward line (Gittens doubtful on top of the counted João Pedro, with Welbeck expected up front) trims their volume a little, so about 23.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.0 shots on target. Same reason, Chelsea short of a fit first-choice forward beyond what is counted: about 8.8.

401879235.overall: A relegation six-pointer: Coventry are 17th under Frank Lampard, two points above bottom side Palace, who have lost four straight league games and have the worst defence in the division. Palace sacked Pierre Sage during the break and this is Thomas Frank's first match in charge, something the numbers can't see. Mateta is banned (three games, counted) and Strand Larsen (ankle) was back in training on Tuesday and could play, otherwise Palace have no recognised centre-forward; Sarr and Tomiyasu were listed with a 21 November return, so their status is unclear. Coventry are missing Haji Wright (counted). Referee Darren England is slightly above average for cards (counted). I lean a little lower on goals for a new manager's first game and a little higher on cards for the stakes.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals, already counting Mateta's ban and Palace's leaky recent defence. A new manager's first game usually starts with a tighter defensive shape, and Palace may be without any fit striker if Strand Larsen isn't ready; Coventry also lack Haji Wright. So a mild trim to about 2.7.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.8 corners. Frank's sides lean on set pieces and direct play, but one week of training won't change Palace's game much, and Coventry's style at home is already in their figures; so I stay at about 8.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, low for a game between 17th and 20th, already counting referee Darren England (4.2 a game). A nervous six-pointer with Palace players trying to impress a new manager usually brings a few more fouls, so a mild lean up to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.2 shots, pushed up by how many shots Palace have been conceding lately. A new manager will first try to stop that, and Palace's own volume suffers if Strand Larsen is missing alongside Mateta; so about 26.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target. Without a recognised striker Palace's shots tend to come from distance, and a more cautious first game under Frank trims it a little, to about 7.8.

401878754.overall: Spurs (11th, 12 pts) host Ipswich (14th, 11 pts) after a 1-0 defeat at Leeds ended a run of three straight wins. Mathys Tel, hurt by a heavy challenge at Leeds, is now described as a major doubt and unlikely to play, which matches the numbers (they already take his goal share off); Xavi Simons and Odobert are long-term out. The good news for Roberto De Zerbi is that Savio, Lucas Bergvall, Mykhailo Mudryk and James Maddison are all reported close to returning, though probably from the bench for most of them. Ipswich, under Gary O'Neil, are winless in four (two draws, two defeats, conceding in all of them); I found no Ipswich team news after a real search, so their side of this view rests on form. Referee Robert Jones (4.3 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already taking about 6% off Spurs for Tel, who is still unlikely to play. What they can't see is Spurs getting creators back: Maddison (no league minutes since the Chelsea game) and Savio are both in line to return, at least off the bench, against an Ipswich side that has conceded in every game of a four-match winless run. A small nudge up: about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, with Spurs' heavy recent corner count (48 in six) and Ipswich's low one (14 in six) already in the momentum adjustment. Returning wingers like Savio and Mudryk fit Spurs' wide play but are more likely to come off the bench, so nothing pushes this further: about 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already adding about 12% for referee Robert Jones (4.3 cards a game) and Ipswich's slightly higher card count lately. There's no derby edge, no suspension story and nothing new on discipline from either camp, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, already adding about 15% to Spurs for their 104 shots in the last six games. Maddison and Savio returning would add quality more than extra volume, and the numbers have already pushed Spurs' shot count high, so I keep 28.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Maddison's shooting from distance and Savio's chance creation, both expected back in the squad, should turn a few more Spurs efforts on target than the side that played without them before the break: about 9.0.

401879232.overall: Leaders Arsenal (27 pts, five straight league wins) visit 12th-placed Newcastle, who have one win in six in all competitions and a manager, Matthias Jaissle, described as under fire. Arsenal's recent wins have been tight (1-0 at Anfield, 1-0 v Hull); Saka (quad, back in December) and the suspended Max Dowman are already counted by the numbers, Martin Zubimendi is a doubt after grabbing his hamstring with Spain, and Christos Tzolis had a clear scan but may start on the bench. Arsenal host Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League three days later. For Newcastle, Joelinton (thigh) and goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen are out as the numbers assume; Willock and Nico Gonzalez should be over illness and Jacob Ramsey is back from a ban. Referee Chris Kavanagh (4.5 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already taking about 11% off Arsenal for Saka. Arsenal have been winning narrowly, Zubimendi is a doubt and Tzolis may only be on the bench, with Dortmund three days later, while Newcastle have scored only 13 league goals; that points a little lower: about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners. Both sides are set-piece threats and Arsenal tend to pin teams back, but that is already in their ratings and recent counts (Arsenal 36 corners in six), and no team news changes how they play, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, already adding about 21% for referee Chris Kavanagh (4.5 cards a game) plus both sides' busier recent card counts. A home crowd frustrated with Jaissle could raise the temperature, but I found nothing concrete beyond that, so I stay at 5.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.5 shots. Newcastle's counter-attacks through Barnes, Murphy and Osula against Arsenal's high line and Arsenal's control of the ball pull in different directions, and the numbers already count Newcastle conceding plenty of shots lately; I keep 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.8 shots on target, already lowered about 6% for Newcastle's poor recent accuracy (21 on target in six). With Saka out and Havertz leading the line, nothing new changes Arsenal's quality of chances, so I stay at 7.8.

401879234.overall: Second-placed Brighton (22 pts, most goals and best goal difference in the league, seven clean sheets) visit Hull (13th), who are eight league games without a win and have drawn their last four at home after leading in several. For Brighton, Mitoma is unlikely after all (Hurzeler said he may need one or two more weeks), so the numbers' assumption that he is out still holds; Ferguson is out, Tzimas is back training, and Struijk is managed day by day. Hull's top scorer Mohamed Belloumi is working back from a hamstring problem (one tracker gives him a 75% chance) and centre-back Nobel Mendy came back from Senegal with a knee knock; Morita, Ansah, Hughes and Gyabi are listed out as the numbers assume. Referee Peter Bankes is about league-average on cards and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and assume Belloumi, Hull's top scorer, is fit; he is still working back from a hamstring problem and may not be sharp, and Hull failed to score in their last two away games. Brighton's expected Mitoma return now looks unlikely, so the earlier reason to go higher has gone: about 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners, with Hull's recent rise in corners (31 in six) already counted. Brighton's width through De Cuyper and Gomez is part of their ratings, and Mitoma's absence was already assumed, so I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already counting Brighton's busier recent card count and referee Peter Bankes, who is close to the league average (about 4 cards a game). Nothing new on discipline from either side, so I stay at 3.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, already adding about 8% for Brighton's high recent shot count. Hull's competitive home form and Brighton's dominance are both already in the ratings, and Brighton's lineup looks settled after the break, so I keep 27.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Hull's for their poor recent accuracy (16 on target in six). A less-than-sharp Belloumi would weigh on that a little, but Brighton's finishing is unchanged without Mitoma, so I stay at 8.2.

401878755.overall: Liverpool (4th, 18 pts) host Manchester United (18th, no league win in five) in the derby, and the big news is that Mauricio Pochettino has replaced Michael Carrick: this is his first game in charge (three outlets report it). Andoni Iraola's Liverpool have doubts over Virgil van Dijk (pulled out of Netherlands duty), Ryan Gravenberch (heel, day to day), Szoboszlai (knee) and Frimpong (hamstring), with Ekitike, Bradley and Leoni out as the numbers assume. United are without Sesko, Baleba and Ugarte; Rashford and Shaw are pushing to return, Dorgu was sent home from Denmark duty and Maguire had back spasms, while Lisandro Martinez is back from a ban. Both teams play in the Champions League three days later; the derby boost to cards and referee Samuel Barrott are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, already adding about 4% to Liverpool for United's leaky defence (16 conceded in six). A new manager's first game usually starts with shape and organisation, and Pochettino at Anfield is likely to be cautious; a possible van Dijk absence pushes the other way, so only a small step down: about 3.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners. A more compact United might give Liverpool more of the ball, but Frimpong's possible absence takes some width from Liverpool's right; nothing clearly points either way, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already adding about 39% for the derby, a little for referee Samuel Barrott (4.1 cards a game) and United's high recent card count. A new manager may bring more pressing and intensity, but the derby boost is already large, so I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.7 shots, already adding about 12% to United for their busy recent attacking under Carrick (96 shots in six). In Pochettino's first game away at Anfield they are more likely to sit in a tighter block and shoot less: about 30.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.8 shots on target. Same reason: a more cautious United under their new manager, with Sesko out and Rashford short of fitness, should make fewer efforts on target: about 9.5.

401875056.overall: Como (5th, four wins in five, 19 goals in their last six) host Cagliari (9th, who ended a run of four defeats by beating Frosinone 1-0 before the break). Fabregas is still without Diao (out since mid-October, so his absence is already in Como's recent form), Addai, Jesus Rodriguez and Kean, but Chalobah is expected back; Perrone, Nico Paz and Da Cunha only rejoin on Thursday from international duty, and Como play in the Champions League next week. The earlier view had Cagliari's defence weakened by an Obert ban; the latest reports list no suspensions and say Mina and Obert have trained with the group and expect to be available, while Fadera and Winks still train apart and Nzola, Aurelio and Trepy are close but not cleared. Referee Andrea Calzavara has a low card record, which the numbers already count, so this view now stays with the numbers on every stat.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals, already lifted for Como's hot run (+6%) and cut for Nzola (-12% on Cagliari's goals) and Fadera being out. I drop last view's small lean up: Mina and Obert are back in training and no Cagliari player is banned, so their back line is not weaker than the numbers think, and Nzola being close to a return is too uncertain to count. I stay at about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.1 corners, mostly Como's (5.9) as they keep the ball against a Cagliari side that switches between a back three and a back four and sits deep away from home. Nothing in the team news changes how either side gets to the byline, so I stay at about 9.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards and already count Calzavara's low rate (3.0 a game) and both teams' quiet recent run (Como only 4 cards in six games). There is no rivalry here, no suspension threat reported and nothing new on the referee, so I stay at about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.4 shots, with Como taking about 18. Perrone, Paz and Da Cunha return late from international duty and Como have a Champions League game next week, which could mean a touch of rotation, but Chalobah's return and Cagliari's recovering defence leave nothing clear either way; I stay at about 26.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target, already raised for Como's sharp recent shooting (+13%). With Mina and Obert likely back for Cagliari, I no longer see a reason to push it higher and stay at about 9.1.

401874981.overall: Leaders Lazio (29 points, one ahead of Inter, unbeaten in five) host Lecce (14th, 10 points, one win in five), who need points to stay clear of the bottom three. Gattuso has a small injury crisis: Zaccagni is now expected to miss out (the latest reports reverse the 18 Nov hint that he was available), and Nuno Tavares, Sutalo and Marusic are out, all as the numbers assume. Frattesi's scan showed only fatigue and he is a real doubt to be decided on Friday, while Gudmundsson is expected back per DAZN (one club-news site says he still has some back pain); the numbers count both as out, so I lean mildly up on Lazio's attack. Lecce are without Pierotti, Ilic and probably Monteiro (counted); referee Matteo Marcenaro's high card rate is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.1 goals after cutting Lazio for Zaccagni (-10.5%), Frattesi (-9.4%), Tavares and Gudmundsson being out. Zaccagni is indeed out, but Frattesi has no injury and could play, and Gudmundsson is expected back, so the numbers take a little too much off Lazio. A mild lean up to about 2.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners. Without Zaccagni and Tavares, Lazio lose two of their most direct left-sided players, while Lecce have won plenty of corners lately (33 in six); the numbers already see both trends, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards and already add Marcenaro's high rate (4.5 a game, +19%) while taking some off for Lazio's calm recent run. Lecce fighting near the bottom away at the leaders could mean some tactical fouls, but there is no rivalry or ban threat reported, so I stay at about 5.

shots.text: The numbers say 25.7 shots. If Frattesi starts and Gudmundsson returns, both counted out, Lazio gain runners who shoot from midfield and the edge of the box; a small nudge to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. The same possible returns of Frattesi and Gudmundsson lift Lazio's threat a little, while Lecce's recent shooting (34 on target in six) is already counted; about 9.0.

401874967.overall: Parma (16th, one win in five) host Roma (3rd, 27 points, three straight wins, 21 goals in their last six). Gilardino is short at the back: Ndiaye is suspended and Romero out (both counted), but Diego Carlos is also out with an adductor strain and Drobnic is doubtful with plantar fasciitis, which the numbers don't know; Troilo is one booking from a ban. Gasperini gets Dybala (to start per Sky), Svilar, Koné and Mancini back, with only Pellegrini and Rensch missing, though one report says Roma play at PSG in the Champions League on Wednesday, so some rotation is possible. Referee Simone Sozza's above-average card rate is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals and already take Romero off Parma (-14%) and lift Roma for their scoring run. Parma's patched-up back three without Diego Carlos (and maybe Drobnic) facing a Roma attack with Dybala back is something the numbers can't see; a possible eye on PSG on Wednesday keeps the lean mild, about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already add Roma's strong recent corner count (+9%). Roma's wing-backs Wesley and Molina push high in Gasperini's 3-4-2-1, but that is in the numbers, so I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already add Sozza's record (4.2 a game). Troilo playing on a booking from a ban may make him a little careful; nothing else new, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already raised a lot for Roma's recent shooting (+26%). Parma's weakened defence points up but possible rotation before PSG points down, and the numbers are already high, so I stay at about 30.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.4 shots on target. Dybala's return gives Roma more quality in the final third against a Parma back line missing Diego Carlos and Ndiaye; a small nudge to about 9.7.

401875067.overall: Napoli (10th, 15 points, one win in five) host Torino (11th, 14 points) in a mid-table game, with Allegri's side facing a Champions League game next week. Napoli's list is long: Lobotka, Di Lorenzo, Badiashile and Alisson Santos (counted) plus Buongiorno, out since knee surgery and so already in their recent form; Neres and Favasuli are expected back but only gradually, and Spinazzola is day to day. Torino's main doubt is Vlasic (counted as out), while Abate gets Belghali, Fortini, Ricardo Rodriguez and Mandragora back. Referee Antonio Rapuano's very high card rate (5.1 a game) is already in the numbers, so the view stays with them.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals, already cut for Lobotka, Di Lorenzo and Vlasic and raised for Napoli's leaky defence lately (14 conceded in six). Neres coming back helps Napoli's attack but likely from the bench, and Torino's returns at the back (Rodriguez, Belghali) point the other way, so I stay at about 2.6.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.4 corners. Napoli have won few corners lately (21 in six) but Torino concede plenty; Neres's return could add width late on, which is not enough to move it, so I stay at about 9.4.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards and already add Rapuano's high rate (+32%). There is no rivalry or ban threat reported and both sides have been calm lately, so I stay at about 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.8 shots, already lifted for Torino's shooting against a Napoli side conceding many chances. Napoli's absences in midfield (Lobotka) and at the back are counted, and Allegri may manage minutes before the Champions League, so nothing clearly moves it; about 27.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target. McTominay, De Bruyne and Hojlund are expected to start and Neres is back as an option, all close to what the numbers assume, so I stay at about 8.8.

401875008.overall: Juventus (7th, 18 pts, LWLWD) host 19th-placed Venezia in the Sunday lunch game, under pressure to win after dropping points to lower-table sides. Spalletti gets Francisco Conceicao back from a shoulder dislocation (full training since last week), but Zhegrova and Celik came back from international duty with muscle complaints, Cambiaso and Nico Gonzalez are still training apart, and Yildiz (out since August, so already absent from the numbers' recent games), Kalulu, Locatelli, Thuram and Grabara are out; the numbers already count Zhegrova, Kalulu and Locatelli as missing. Venezia have a new coach, Davide Nicola, who has started to get results (a 1-0 win over Napoli) and whose teams usually defend deep and fight; Franjic and Sverko are out, Mazzocchi is a serious doubt and striker Adorante is only back in training. Referee Alberto Arena has a low card record on a tiny sample, which the numbers already blend in.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals and already take about 11% off Juventus for Zhegrova, who most outlets still list as out or unlikely to start, so that stays as is. Conceicao's return is not on the numbers' list and his recent absence dragged on Juventus's form, so a small lean higher to about 2.47; Nicola's deep-lying Venezia stop me going further.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.9 corners, already lifted about 12% by Juventus's recent corner count. Against a Nicola side that will sit in its own half, Juventus should pile up corners, but that is what the numbers already expect, so I stay at 10.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 2.8 cards, cut by both teams' quiet recent card counts and by Arena's low record (1.7 per game in only 3 games), all already counted. Venezia under new coach Nicola are in a relegation fight and will defend deep and physically against a Juventus side that must win, so a mild lean higher to about 2.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.4 shots, with Venezia's recent shooting already adding about 18% to their side. Conceicao, a dribbler who shoots often, is back for Juventus and was not part of their recent games, so a small nudge to about 31.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Juventus have been poor at hitting the target lately (23 in their last 6, which the numbers already count), and Conceicao's return gives them a bit more quality in the final third, so about 9.2.

401875047.overall: In-form Bologna (8th, four straight wins under Palladino) host bottom side Udinese, who sacked Runjaic on 2 November after eight games without a win and are now coached by Paolo Zanetti, who has had the international break to work with the squad. Bologna miss Holm and Enem and also left-back Juan Miranda (hamstring, back around end of November), their main assist provider, who is not on the numbers' list; Cambiaghi, counted as out, is in a race to be fit after an ankle knock with Italy (reports split). Udinese miss Gueye and Bertola (both counted), while Alaba and Zanoli are close to returning. Referee Livio Marinelli's average card record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, already lifted by Bologna's 13 goals in their last 6 and Udinese's leaky defence, and already cut for Cambiaghi and Gueye. Miranda's absence takes away much of Bologna's creativity down the left, and Zanetti is expected to keep a back three that drops into a five, with two weeks to organise it, so a mild lean lower to about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.5 corners. Bologna should have most of the ball against a deep Udinese, which can bring corners, but losing Miranda's crossing works the other way, so nothing points clearly either way and I stay at 9.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards and already count Marinelli's average record (3.6 per game in 27 games) and Udinese's quiet recent card count. A bottom side under a new coach may defend more aggressively, but Bologna are a calm, possession side, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, already lifted by both teams' recent shooting. Without Miranda's deliveries and against a Udinese side likely set up to defend in numbers under Zanetti, Bologna may find fewer clean chances, so a small cut to about 25.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.8 shots on target, already lifted 16% by Bologna's sharp recent finishing. Orsolini and Bernardeschi are expected to start and Udinese have conceded plenty on target lately, so I see no reason to move from 8.8.

401874960.overall: Sassuolo (17th, five straight defeats) sacked Alberto Aquilani and appointed Roberto D'Aversa, whose first game this is; his stated priority is solidity: shorter distances between the lines, protecting the goal and defending transitions. Berardi and Volpato, counted as out by the numbers, are doubtful but could make it (training this week decides), and Adzic, also counted out, picked up a knee problem with Montenegro. Genoa (13th) under De Rossi have almost the whole squad available, with only Frendrup (ankle) a doubt, and lost their last game to Milan through two defensive errors. Referee Maria Sole Ferrieri Caputi's average card record is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.5 goals, already cut hard for Adzic, Berardi and Volpato, and already lifted for Genoa by Sassuolo conceding 20 in their last 6. The previous view leaned higher on one report that Berardi and Volpato were back, but the latest news (Sky, fantacalcio.it, 18 Nov) still lists both as doubtful, while a new coach focused first on defending usually tightens things in his first game, so I now lean lower to about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.9 corners. D'Aversa's more compact Sassuolo may concede fewer chances but not necessarily fewer corners, and Genoa's corner count has been low lately, which the numbers already count, so I stay at 8.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards and already count Ferrieri Caputi's record (4.0 per game) and Sassuolo's quiet recent card count. A desperate home side in its first game under a new coach, with a relegation fight starting, usually plays with more edge, so a mild lean higher to about 4.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.7 shots. D'Aversa wants a tighter block and fewer transitions, and Sassuolo have been shooting little lately (53 in 6, already counted), so with Berardi doubtful I expect a slightly cagier game, about 23.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.3 shots on target, with Sassuolo already low (14 on target in 6) and Genoa lifted by Sassuolo's leaky defence. A more compact Sassuolo should give Genoa fewer clear looks, so a small cut to about 8.1.

401874989.overall: Milan (4th, 24 pts) host surprise side Frosinone (6th, 20 pts), who have been scoring and shooting a lot lately. Frosinone miss top scorer Raimondo (ankle, out until mid-December), the suspended Bracaglia, and probably Grillitsch and Terzic, all already counted by the numbers. Milan's defence is stretched: Tomori (out since 28 October, back around end of November) and Gabbia are out and Pavlovic is doubtful, while Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze are also out; only Gabbia, Loftus-Cheek, Saelemaekers and Chukwueze are on the numbers' list. Referee Luca Pairetto is one of the strictest in Serie A (4.9 cards per game), which the numbers already add. News for this match was thinner than for others: mostly injury tables and a probable-lineup page, no dedicated preview article.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals and already take about 19% off Frosinone for Raimondo and more for Bracaglia and Terzic. Tomori's absence and the doubt over Pavlovic are not on the numbers' list and leave Milan's back line thin (De Winter and Gila expected), so a mild lean higher to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, with Frosinone's high recent corner count already adding about 10% and Milan's low one taking some off. Nothing in the team news changes how either side gets the ball wide, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already raised about a third for Pairetto's strict record (4.9 per game in 31 games). That is already a high figure for Serie A and neither side has a suspension worry or derby edge, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 33.3 shots, already lifted about 24% on Frosinone's side for their heavy recent shooting (137 in 6). Without Raimondo, whose absence the numbers count only on goals, Frosinone may shoot a little less, while Milan's thin defence could allow more, so these roughly cancel and I stay at 33.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.8 shots on target, already lifted for Frosinone's accurate recent shooting. A Milan defence without Tomori and possibly Pavlovic, not on the numbers' list, is a small reason for about 11.1.

401875541.overall: Mid-table NEC (11th, 14 pts) host leaders PSV (26 pts) after the international break; PSV want to keep the top spot they just took back. NEC come in on a high: Dusan Tadic, out with a calf problem in October, is fit again and scored twice in the 3-2 win at Utrecht on 8 November, and he says most of the injured defenders are back. Still out for NEC are Bram Nuytinck and Dennis Geiger (in the numbers), Emre Mor is doubtful, and two injury trackers also list centre-back Perr Schuurs out with a hamstring problem, which the numbers do not have. PSV miss Nagalo, Schouten and Plea (counted) plus Sami Ouaissa, and the Eindhovens Dagblad reports Sergino Dest and Filip Kostic as doubts; Paul Wanner is a long shot and Ivan Perisic likely fit. Referee Jeroen Manschot's higher card rate is already in the numbers. My earlier view had Tadic out; that was wrong, so I removed that cut.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already including NEC's hot scoring run and the minor absences of Mor, Geiger and Plea. Tadic is fit and scoring again, and NEC are also without centre-back Perr Schuurs, who is not on the numbers' list, which weakens a defence facing PSV's attack; the last five meetings all had three or more goals. A mild +3% to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with NEC's recent corner surge and PSV's quieter spell already in the momentum adjustments. PSV's wide players Sergino Dest and Filip Kostic are both doubts after not playing in the international break; without them PSV lose much of their crossing down the flanks. A small -3% to about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.9 cards, already including Jeroen Manschot's record of 3.5 cards a game (about +18%). No suspensions are hanging over either side and nothing suggests extra tension beyond a normal top-versus-midtable game, so I stay at 3.9.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.4 shots, and NEC's heavy recent shooting (116 in six games) is already in the momentum adjustment. Tadic's return pushes NEC's volume up, but PSV's possible absences on the flanks pull theirs a little down, so the two roughly cancel and I stay at 29.4.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.0 shots on target. NEC's sharper recent finishing is already counted, Tadic is back to create chances, and PSV still have their main scorers; with Dest and Kostic doubtful the picture is mixed, so I stay at 11.0.

401875544.overall: Struggling Utrecht (14th, lost their last two) host Cambuur (10th), who were unbeaten in seven league games before a 2-5 home loss to PSV. Utrecht coach Anthony Correia is under growing pressure; club watchers say a sacking is not on the table yet, but fans and former players are openly critical and local media call Cambuur the favourites. Utrecht are without Kevin Paredes, Miliano Jonathans and Noah Ohio, with Alonzo Engwanda and Victor Jensen doubtful; Cambuur miss first-choice keeper Jasper Meijster (hand, out until March), Wout Asselman and captain Jamal Amofa. Their top scorer Rafik El Arguioui, on loan from Utrecht, played the full game against PSV; I could not confirm whether he is allowed to face his parent club. Referee Allard Lindhout (3.2 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.1 goals, already including Cambuur's good scoring run and Utrecht conceding 15 in six. Cambuur's first-choice keeper Meijster is out until March, which the numbers list but give no goal effect, and Utrecht's back line has been weakened by summer transfer choices; a mild +3% to about 4.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, most of them Utrecht's (6.4). Utrecht under pressure at home should push forward and Cambuur have been happy to defend and counter, but that is already the shape of the numbers, so I stay at 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, already including Utrecht's recent rise in cards (+10%) and Lindhout's slightly above-average record. A nervous home crowd could add some edge, but that is mostly what the momentum figure already shows, so I stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.1 shots. Utrecht shoot a lot (99 in six) but without much accuracy, and Cambuur's attack runs through El Arguioui, Ceka and Binder; with El Arguioui's availability against his parent club unconfirmed, I stay at 29.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.4 shots on target, already including Utrecht's poor accuracy (-6%) and Cambuur's sharper finishing (+8%). A backup keeper in the Cambuur goal changes how many go in more than how many are on target, so I stay at 10.4.

401875543.overall: Second-placed Feyenoord host Excelsior (15th), who have lost five league games in a row, including 0-9 at home to Twente. Feyenoord are winless in four in all competitions, including a 5-3 defeat at Heerenveen (their first league loss) and Champions League defeats, so Giovanni van Bronckhorst needs a response. Their defence is thin: St. Juste (counted by the numbers), Nieuwkoop, Bos, Beelen and Wessels are out and Gijs Smal and Anis Hadj Moussa are 50/50, but attackers Reiss Nelson, Goncalo Borges and Shaqueel van Persie are back. Excelsior's Nesto Groen serves the last game of his ban (counted) and Aymen Sliti is a doubt with a hand injury. The numbers add a big derby boost for cards, but this Rotterdam derby is a lopsided, friendly one (Feyenoord have won 47 of 57 meetings, and Feyenoord welcomed the Excelsior fans warmly), so I trim that.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.9 goals, already counting Excelsior's collapse (22 conceded in six), St. Juste's absence and Groen's ban. Feyenoord get Nelson, Borges and Van Persie back in attack, while a back line missing four or five regulars keeps the door open for Excelsior too; a mild +4% to about 4.1.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Feyenoord taking most of them (6.8) and Excelsior's drop in corners already in the momentum adjustment. Hadj Moussa, Feyenoord's direct winger, is only 50/50, but Nelson and Borges give other wide options, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, and that already includes a +39% derby boost plus referee Robin Hensgens' average record. This city derby is not a hostile one: Feyenoord have dominated it for decades and the clubs' fans get on, and a one-sided game with Feyenoord on the ball usually brings few fouls from the home side. I trim it -6% to about 3.4.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.3 shots, with Feyenoord on 19.2 and Excelsior on just 9.1 after a dismal run (45 shots in six games, already counted). Feyenoord's returning attackers support a high home total, but that is already the numbers' expectation, so I stay at 28.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.9 shots on target, already including Excelsior giving up many on-target shots (+9% for Feyenoord) and barely hitting the target themselves. With Sliti doubtful and Groen banned, Excelsior's threat stays small, and the numbers already see that, so I stay at 10.9.

401875546.overall: The Derby of the North: Groningen (9th, three defeats in four, last a 4-3 loss at AZ) against in-form Heerenveen (6th), who have won four in a row, the last a 5-3 comeback win over Feyenoord. Groningen lost two players to red cards at AZ: keeper Etienne Vaessen (two yellows) and Hans Hateboer (handball on the line) are both banned for this game, the club confirmed, and their other senior keeper Rijk Janse is out long-term with a knee injury; Travis Hernes and Malcolm Jeng are also injured. Heerenveen have a fully fit squad. All of that, the derby and referee Alex Bos' slightly higher card rate are already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.4 goals, already including both teams' scoring runs (17 goals each in six games), Vaessen's ban (+6% for Heerenveen) and Hateboer's absence. Both sides' last games were wild (4-3 and 5-3), which the momentum figures already reflect, so I stay at 3.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.0 corners, with Groningen's recent drop in corners already counted (-6%). Losing right-back Hateboer takes some width from Groningen's right side, but his replacement plays the same role, and Heerenveen with a full squad change nothing, so I stay at 10.0.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards, already including a +39% derby boost and Alex Bos' 3.3 cards a game. This is a genuinely heated rivalry, with fireworks and stoppages in past meetings, but that is exactly what the derby boost covers, so I add nothing and stay at 4.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, already including Heerenveen's rising shot count (+7.5%). Heerenveen in form and Groningen needing a home win in the derby both point to an open game, which is the numbers' starting point, so I stay at 28.8.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, already including Heerenveen's sharper finishing (+7%) and a cut for Groningen against a Heerenveen side that has allowed few on-target shots. A stand-in keeper for Groningen matters for goals more than for shots on target, so I stay at 10.0.

401875539.overall: A relegation-zone game: Telstar (16th, 10 pts) host PEC Zwolle (13th, 12 pts). The big change is on PEC's bench: Alex Pastoor was appointed head coach on 7 November after caretakers led the side for five games, and this is his first match after nearly two weeks of training; the numbers cannot see that. Telstar's Rui Mendes and Gerald Alders are only 25% to play and PEC's Sherel Floranus and Filip Krastev are doubtful, with Givaro Rahajaan out; the numbers already treat them as absent. Referee Joey Kooij (3.4 cards a game) is already counted. News on Telstar's side was thin: their club site and the injury trackers had nothing beyond the injury list.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, already counting Mendes' absence for Telstar (-3.5%) and Alders' for their defence. A new coach's first game, here Pastoor's at PEC, usually brings a more organised and cautious side, and with both teams near the bottom neither can afford to lose; a mild -4% to about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.1 corners, with Telstar's recent drop (-3%) already counted. How Pastoor sets PEC up is not known yet, and nothing in Telstar's news points either way, so I stay at 10.1.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.6 cards, already including Joey Kooij's above-average record (+11%) and PEC's recent card count. A six-pointer near the bottom with a new coach demanding intensity tends to bring more fouls than a normal game, which the numbers do not flag; a small +3% to about 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.1 shots, already including Telstar's recent shooting surge (+11%). A tighter PEC could cut Telstar's chances a little, but that is too unsure to size on shot volume, so I stay at 30.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.6 shots on target. With PEC likely to be harder to play through in Pastoor's first game and Telstar without their attacker Mendes (already counted for goals), clear chances should be a bit scarcer; a small -3% to about 10.3.

401875545.overall: Fourth-placed Twente (24 pts) host bottom side Willem II, who have 3 points from 12 games, have conceded 40 goals and have not won in 29 Eredivisie matches; a draw or defeat would equal the league's worst winless run (Helmond Sport, 1983-84). Willem II sacked John Stegeman on 20 October and Jurgen Streppel has since lost 7-0 at PSV and drawn 1-1 with PEC Zwolle, while Twente come out of the break wanting to bounce back after dropping points at Fortuna and Utrecht last time and drawing 2-2 with Ajax on 8 November. Twente's Thorvaldsen, Bruns, Unnerstall and Lemkin are all still doubtful (25-50% in one injury tracker); the numbers only take a tiny amount off for Bruns. Willem II miss Hoogma and Lachkar, as the numbers know, and one tracker also lists winger Jaden Slory as suspended, which the numbers do not see. Serdar Gozubuyuk's high card rate is already a big part of the cards number.

goals.text: The numbers say 4.0 goals, already lifted for Twente's 21 goals in their last six and Willem II's 21 conceded. The only thing they can't see is Jaden Slory's suspension listed by one injury tracker, a small loss for a side that has scored 11 all season, so I trim Willem II's share slightly to about 3.9. Twente's doubtful attackers (Thorvaldsen, Bruns) returning would not change much, as the numbers barely took them off.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.8 corners, with Twente's 46 corners in their last six already counted and Willem II's low corner output too. Expect Twente to camp in Willem II's half against a side under a new coach that has conceded 40 goals; that one-sided pattern is exactly what the numbers already describe, so I stay at 10.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, and Serdar Gozubuyuk's record (3.9 a game over 80 games) is already a +37% part of it, with Willem II's recent 12 cards in six also counted. A bottom side chasing a first win under Streppel could get stuck in, but that is the usual picture for a relegation side away at a top-four team; I add nothing and stay at 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 35.6 shots, already pushed up a lot (about +25%) for Twente's 145 shots in their last six. Willem II have been shelled recently (0-7 at PSV) and their own shooting is low, which is also counted. No lineup news points either way, so I stay at 35.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 11.2 shots on target, with Twente's recent accuracy already counted. Willem II's attack, already the weakest in the league, loses Slory to a suspension according to one tracker, so I shave their share a little to about 11.0.

401875547.overall: Third-placed Ajax host ADO Den Haag (17th), who sacked Robin Peter on 2 November and won 3-1 against Sparta under interim coach Levi Schwiebbe. The numbers have taken a big cut off Ajax for Julian Brandt (-13%) and Kasper Dolberg (-7%); Dolberg is out for the season, but Brandt (hamstring) has a good chance of playing according to Ajax Showtime and is rated 50% by an injury tracker, with Berghuis, Gaaei and Kehrer also 50/50 and Tsygankov and Adingra unlikely. ADO still miss Alex Pozo and Luka Reischl, as the numbers know, and keeper Kilian Nikiema (50%), Yannick Eduardo (25%) and Pascal Mulder (75%) are doubts the numbers do not see. Ajax host FC Thun in the Conference League on Thursday and go to Feyenoord next Sunday, so some rotation is possible, but Míchel is likely to field a strong side at home. Referee Erwin Blank shows slightly fewer cards than average, which is already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, but they take Ajax down 13% as if Brandt is surely out; reports say he has a good chance of returning, so I give back roughly half of that on Ajax's side. ADO's first-choice keeper Nikiema is also only 50/50, which the numbers don't see. Together that moves me to about 3.3 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, with Ajax's slightly low recent corner count and ADO's normal output already counted. ADO's change of coach and Brandt's possible return don't change how the game is likely to look: Ajax with the ball, ADO defending deep. I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, already trimmed about 5% for Erwin Blank's slightly low card rate (3.0 a game) and nudged up for both teams' recent bookings. A relegation-threatened ADO under an interim coach may play with edge, but nothing beyond what the numbers already see; I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 34.1 shots, with both sides' recent shooting already counted. Brandt, Berghuis and Gaaei all being close to a return gives Ajax more creative options than the numbers assume, so I lean slightly higher, to about 35.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. With Brandt likely back in some role and ADO possibly without their first-choice keeper, Ajax should test the goal a little more than the numbers assume; about 10.8.

401875540.overall: Sparta (12th, 12 pts) host AZ (5th, 23 pts), who have won only one of their last five league games (a 4-3 win over Groningen) after a strong start under Lee-Roy Echteld, and who are also playing in the Europa League. AZ's absences go beyond what the numbers know: besides Hornkamp, Zoet and Resink (counted), Kees Smit is out again for weeks with a groin setback (NOS, AZ Fanpage), and Weslley Patati and Lewis Schouten are listed injured, with Wouter Goes not fit; Smit has played only 57 league minutes this season, so his loss is mostly already in the team's numbers. Sparta lost 3-1 at ADO before the break; one injury tracker lists Michael Brouwer and Nick Verschuren out and Julian Baas doubtful, which the numbers do not see and which I could not confirm elsewhere. Referee Ingmar Oostrom's slightly above-average card rate is already counted. News for this specific match is thin during the international break; this view rests mostly on the injury lists and form.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already taking about 5% off AZ for Hornkamp and counting Sparta's 16 conceded in their last six. AZ's extra absences (Patati, Schouten, Smit) are squad players this season and Sparta's listed absences are unconfirmed, so they roughly cancel out; I stay at 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.6 corners, with AZ's low corners conceded and Sparta's normal output already counted. Nothing in the team news changes how wide either side plays, so I stay at 10.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards, already pushed up for Sparta's 14 cards in their last six and for Ingmar Oostrom (3.3 a game). Nothing new on discipline, suspensions or the referee, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, with AZ's recent 93 shots in six counted. AZ are short of attacking depth: winger Patati, Schouten and the creative Smit are out on top of Hornkamp, and an AZ side with European games around it may be a bit flatter, so I trim slightly to about 28.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.1 shots on target, already lifted a little for AZ's accuracy against a Sparta side that concedes plenty of efforts. With fewer options in AZ's attack than the numbers assume, I shade it to about 9.9.

401875542.overall: Go Ahead Eagles (8th, 17 pts) host Fortuna Sittard (7th, 20 pts), who have drawn four of their last five. Fortuna are badly hit: Ole Romeny, Edouard Michut, Daley Sinkgraven, Lequincio Zeefuik and Rodrigo Guth were all out for the 2-2 with Telstar (club news site Fortuna Online), and an injury tracker still lists all of them, plus Ramazan Bayram, out until December or January; the brief lists no Fortuna absences, so the numbers do not see them, although their recent momentum partly reflects the weaker side. Fortuna Online also reports (18 November) that coach Danny Buijs will not extend his contract. Go Ahead won 1-0 at Excelsior last time with Jasper Cillessen in goal; Marsman and Saathof are out as the numbers know. Referee Martijn Vos (4.6 cards a game) is already a large part of the cards number.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Fortuna are without forwards Romeny and Zeefuik and midfielders Michut and Sinkgraven, none of whom the numbers take off, and they have scored only 8 in their last six (partly counted in momentum). I trim Fortuna's attack and land at about 2.9 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.5 corners, already cut a little for Fortuna's low recent corner count (20 in six). Go Ahead's settled side (same XI two games running) should press in the usual way, and Fortuna's absences are already showing in that low corner count, so I stay at 10.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.7 cards: Martijn Vos's very high card rate (+40%) pushes it up, while Go Ahead's 4 cards in their last six and Fortuna's low count pull it down, all already counted. Buijs's contract news is unlikely to change how either side plays, so I stay at 3.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.6 shots. Fortuna's shooting is down recently (64 in six) and they are missing several attacking players the numbers don't know about, so I lean lower to about 26.5.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.7 shots on target. With Romeny, Zeefuik and Michut out, Fortuna should test Go Ahead's keeper less than the numbers assume; about 9.3.

401875001.overall: Atalanta (12th, 14 pts, one win in five) host second-placed Inter (28 pts, four wins in five) after the international break, with Sarri's side well short of last season's level and Chivu's Inter chasing the top spot. Inter's attack is thin: Lautaro Martinez is back in group training after a hamstring strain since 13 October and may start, Thuram came home from France duty with fatigue and is day to day, Bonny is out about three more weeks and Esposito is being checked; none of this is in the numbers, which list no missing players. Atalanta expect Raspadori, Kristensen, Bellanova and Gaetano back (maybe not for full minutes), while centre-backs Hien and Kossounou were still not reported fit. Inter host Stuttgart in the Champions League three days later and Chivu plans to share minutes between Lautaro and Thuram. One fixture site listed Calhanoglu as suspended, but the official matchday 12 suspension and booking-warning list (17 Nov) has no Inter or Atalanta player, so I treat him as available; no referee named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, 2.0 of them for Inter. I lean mildly lower to about 2.9: Inter arrive with a patched-up attack (Lautaro just back after five weeks out, Thuram doubtful with fatigue, Bonny out) and Chivu plans to split minutes between his strikers before the Stuttgart game. Atalanta's leaky recent defence (12 conceded in six) is already in the numbers through momentum, so I don't count it again.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.6 corners, with Inter's recent rise in corners (36 in six) and Atalanta conceding many already counted through momentum. Atalanta's wing-backs Bellanova and Kristensen returning should help them push wide at home, while Inter's thinner attack points the other way, so nothing clearly moves it; I stay at 9.6.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.1 cards and already add for the past meetings (head-to-head +13% on Atalanta's side) and for Atalanta's recent cards against. No referee has been named yet and neither side has anyone on a booking warning, so I find nothing the numbers miss and stay at 3.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.8 shots, with Inter on 16.3 after a +10% momentum boost for their recent shooting. I trim slightly to about 27.9 because Inter's front line is short of fitness (Lautaro returning, Thuram doubtful, Bonny out) and minutes are likely to be managed before the Champions League; Atalanta getting Raspadori back is a small offset.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target, 5.4 of them Inter's. For the same reason as goals, a rusty Lautaro and a doubtful Thuram with Bonny out, I lean mildly lower to about 8.9; Atalanta conceding plenty lately is already in the numbers.

401876400.overall: Marseille are 4th and have won five Ligue 1 games in a row under Bruno Genesio (2-1 at Lens last time out), while promoted Le Mans are 15th with 8 points and one win in their last six (1-1 with Monaco before the break). Marseille are without left-back Emerson (knee operation) and defender Derek Cornelius (hip, out until the end of the year); Le Mans miss attacking midfielder Adil Bourabaa (ankle surgery) and right-back Djibril Sidibé (broken foot), with Samuel Yohou a doubt after a head knock. None of these absences is on the numbers' missing list, but all have been out for weeks, so recent form already reflects most of them. Marseille host Levski Sofia in the Europa League on Thursday 26 November, so some rotation or game management is possible, and the upper Virage Sud will be closed after an LFP sanction. No referee was named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.6 goals, 2.6 of them Marseille's, already boosted a little for their 14 goals in the last six. I lean slightly lower to about 3.5: Emerson's absence takes away an attacking left-back, and with Levski Sofia coming on Thursday Genesio may rotate or ease off once ahead. Le Mans' missing creator Bourabaa has been out since October, so that is mostly in their form already.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.1 corners and already take a little off for both sides' low corner counts lately (Le Mans won 18 in six against 24 expected). Emerson's absence could mean fewer overlaps on the left, but Marseille should still have most of the ball against a side near the bottom, so nothing clearly points either way and I stay at about 8.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.1 cards, with more expected from Le Mans, who have picked up 16 cards in their last six and are usually chasing the ball in games like this; the numbers already count that form. No referee has been named yet, and it is not a derby or a heated fixture, so I stay at about 4.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 26 shots, about 15 for Marseille and 11 for Le Mans. Marseille's winning run and Le Mans' struggles are in the form figures already, and the possible rotation before the Europa League game is too uncertain to size, so I stay at about 26.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target and already trim Marseille's for their recent 24 in six (30 expected). Gouiri remains Marseille's main scorer and no new absence hits either attack beyond what has been out for weeks, so I stay at about 9.

401882803.overall: Getafe (15th, 12 pts) host Atlético Madrid (3rd, 28 pts) on Sunday night, the first league game after the international break. Getafe have taken all their points at the Coliseum but have not scored in six away games; Gudelj is banned (the numbers count it) and Uche (out for the season since August), Juanmi and Zaid Romero are also out. Atlético have lost Lookman to a mild knee sprain picked up with Nigeria (about two weeks, per two reports), which the numbers do not know about, while Cuti Romero is a serious doubt and Pubill has ankle discomfort. Simeone had about 17 internationals away, some back late in the week, and a Champions League game against Viking follows on Tuesday, so some rotation or caution is possible. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.2 goals, already counting Gudelj's ban, recent form and past meetings. I lean a little lower: Atlético lose Lookman, one of their main attacking outlets, which the numbers do not know about, their internationals return late with a Champions League game on Tuesday, and Bordalás's Getafe make games slow and tight at home. So about 2.1 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.3 corners and already count Getafe's high recent corner count (38 in six games) and past meetings. Getafe play direct and win corners from long balls and crosses at home, while Atlético without Lookman have a bit less pace out wide, but nothing points clearly either way. I stay at about 9.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.3 cards, counting both teams' card form and past meetings, but the game is not flagged as a derby. Getafe against Atlético is a local Madrid game against a Bordalás side built on fouls, duels and time-wasting, and these meetings tend to get heated. With no referee named yet, I lean mildly higher, to about 5.6.

shots.text: The numbers say 24.6 shots, and recent form has already pushed both sides up (+13% Getafe, +8% Atlético). Getafe managed only 9 shots at Villarreal last time out and rely on long balls, and Atlético will be without Lookman and are likely to manage the game before Tuesday's Champions League match. I lean lower, to about 23.1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 7.4 shots on target. Getafe have not scored away for six games but are more dangerous at home, and Atlético lose some quality up front with Lookman out and Cuti Romero doubtful at the back changes little for this stat. I lean slightly lower, to about 7.0.

401883111.overall: Sixth-placed Burgos (24 pts) host 19th-placed Albacete (13 pts) on Sunday night at El Plantío. Burgos, under Sergio Francisco, saw a four-game unbeaten run end with a 3-1 loss at Leganés built on defensive errors; they are without forward Jon Karrikaburu and David González (hamstrings), absences the numbers do not know about. Albacete have been transformed since Joseba Etxeberria replaced Alberto González in October: one point from eight games before, four straight league wins since (latest 1-0 v Celta Fortuna), with a high press and quick counters, though still in the bottom four. Albacete are missing Antonio Puertas, Samu Obeng, Fran Gámez, Higinio Marín, Gyabaa and the suspended José Corpas, with Javi Moreno doubtful; most of those have been out for weeks, so recent form already reflects them. No referee named yet; news on line-ups was thin beyond injury lists.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals. Albacete's attack is still blunt (striker Soberón has no league goal and missed a penalty last week) but their press has turned them into a team that wins tight games, while Burgos lose a forward in Karrikaburu and leaked three at Leganés. Those pull in opposite directions and the numbers' momentum already counts both sides' recent scoring (+1-3%), so I stay at 2.3.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.9 corners, already raised for Burgos' heavy recent corner count (+6.7% momentum). Albacete under Etxeberria spend long spells defending after scoring and lean on counters, which fits Burgos pushing for corners at home; that is what the numbers already show, so I stay at 9.9.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already up about 9% each side for recent card counts (Albacete 21 in their last six). Albacete's aggressive press and Burgos' frustration after Leganés point to a lively game, but that is what the momentum figures capture and no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.2 shots, with Burgos' side pushed up 23% for a run of high shot counts. I lean slightly lower, to about 25.2: Burgos are without forward Jon Karrikaburu (hamstring), which the numbers do not know, and Albacete's new high press under Etxeberria has made them harder to play through than their season averages suggest.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.0 shots on target, Burgos' share already raised about 9% for recent form. For the same reasons as shots, Karrikaburu's absence and Albacete's improved, pressing defence (three clean sheets in four league wins), I trim it mildly to about 7.8.

401883110.overall: Bottom against top at the Alfonso Murube on Monday night: Ceuta are last with 5 points from 14 games, eight from safety, and lost 2-0 at Tenerife in Sergio Lobera's first game after José Juan Romero was sacked. Almería, under Xavier García Pimienta, lead with 32 points, are unbeaten in 11 and have the best defence (11 conceded), with Miguel de la Fuente the league's top scorer on nine. Lobera now has a full week to bring in his possession and pressing ideas; at Tenerife Ceuta had about 64% of the ball but few clear chances and conceded on a counter and from a corner. Almería get Marcos Luna back from a ban and Dzodic and Cipenga back from international duty, with only Ely and Melamed out; Ceuta's Edgar Sevikyan went off injured at Tenerife with no update since. No referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.3 goals, 1.2 of them Ceuta's, helped by last season's 3-2 home win in the head-to-head. I lean slightly lower, to about 3.2: Ceuta have scored 10 in 14 and under Lobera had the ball at Tenerife but little presence in the box, Sevikyan is a doubt after going off injured, and Almería have conceded only 11 all season. Almería's own scoring (De la Fuente in form, 13 in their last six) is already in the numbers.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners, 6.1 of them Ceuta's, which already includes their recent run of winning lots of corners (+11.4% momentum). Lobera's possession style fits that pattern rather than changing it, and Almería tend to let opponents have the ball, so I stay at 9.8.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.0 cards, already counting Ceuta's heavy recent booking (+12% momentum). Ceuta are desperate and at Tenerife were booked for stopping counters when their press was beaten, which is the same pattern; no referee has been named yet, so I stay at 6.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.3 shots, with Ceuta's recent shot volume already adding a large 30% to their side. Under Lobera they kept the ball and shot from range (Kuki Zalazar), while Almería tend to need few chances; that fits what the numbers already expect, so I stay at 31.3.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.3 shots on target. In line with my goals lean I take a little off, to about 10.0: Ceuta managed only two on target at Tenerife despite most of the ball, their shooting is mostly from distance, and Sevikyan may be missing; Almería's own accuracy and their solid defence are already in the numbers.

401875009.overall: A meeting of two struggling sides on Monday night: Monza (Ivan Juric) are 18th with 7 points and have lost four of their last five, while Fiorentina (Paolo Vanoli) are 15th with 9 points after three games unbeaten (2-2 Atalanta, 4-2 Sassuolo, 2-2 Juventus). Both have scored 17 and conceded 25 in 11 games, so open, leaky games are the norm for both. Monza rely on Gustavo Varela, the league's top scorer; Folorunsho is back from a calf problem, but captain Pessina, Robinson (muscle problem from England U20 duty), Ngonge, Ciurria and Mout carry fitness doubts. Fiorentina miss Pongracic and Parisi, Atta and Ndour are close to returning, and Njie came back from Sweden duty with a thigh knock (Gnonto would replace him). The brief lists no missing players for either side, and no referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.2 goals, and they already add a little for both sides' recent scoring and leaky defending (+2.6% each way). Both teams average about 3.8 goals per game between them this season, but knocks to attackers on both sides (Robinson and Ngonge for Monza, Njie for Fiorentina) and the relegation tension pull the other way, so I stay at 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.5 corners, already nudging up for Fiorentina's recent corner count. Monza's wing-back 3-4-2-1 (Birindelli and Mangas wide) and Fiorentina's 4-2-3-1 don't point either way beyond what the numbers see, so I stay at 8.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.8 cards, with recent card form already counted and no referee named yet. This is a scrap near the bottom: Monza are in the relegation zone and a win would lift them past Fiorentina, and the brief carries no stakes flag for it, so I lean mildly higher, to about 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.9 shots, already raised strongly for both sides' recent shooting (+9% Monza, +13% Fiorentina). With Monza's supporting attackers Robinson and Ngonge and Fiorentina's Njie all carrying knocks, and Fiorentina's six internationals back only late in the week, I trim it slightly to about 28.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.0 shots on target, already lifted around 10% for each side's recent form. For the same reasons as shots (attacking knocks on both sides, late returns from international duty) I trim it slightly to about 9.7; Varela, Monza's main threat, is fit and starts.

401879237.overall: Brentford (8th, 14 pts) host Everton (6th, 16 pts) on Monday night after the international break, two mid-table sides with only two points between them. Brentford lost 2-0 at Brighton last time after Igor Thiago, their main striker, was sent off for violent conduct; the appeal was rejected and his three-match ban starts here, which the numbers already count. Brentford are also without Rico Henry, Josh Dasilva and Kaye Furo, while Fabio Carvalho was ruled out until after the break and may be back. Everton came from behind to beat Coventry 3-1 with Thierno Barry scoring twice, report no injuries, and Jack Grealish is back in training after a disciplinary absence but David Moyes has not said whether he will play. No referee had been named when this was written.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.4 goals. Without Thiago Brentford have no obvious centre-forward (predicted line-ups leave the slot open, with Schade the likeliest to move inside), but the numbers already take his absence off, about -12.5% on Brentford's goals. Grealish could give Everton more craft if he returns, but his place is not confirmed, so I stay at 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners. Brentford have won fewer corners than usual in their last six (21 against about 28 expected) and Everton a few more, which the numbers already count through form. I found nothing in the team news that changes how either side will attack wide, so I stay at 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.5 cards, with Everton slightly more likely to pick them up. No referee had been named, so the numbers use average refereeing, and recent card form and past meetings are already counted. Nothing in the build-up points to a bad-tempered game, so I stay at 3.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. They take Thiago's ban off Brentford's goals but not off their shots, and he is the side's main shot-taker with no like-for-like replacement while Carvalho is only just coming back. Grealish's possible return pulls a little the other way for Everton, so I lean only mildly lower: about 26.9.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target. Brentford have already been hitting the target less than usual (19 in their last six against about 25 expected), which the numbers count, and losing Thiago, their most direct finisher, should cut that a little more. I go mildly lower, to about 8.0.

401882802.overall: A Monday-night relegation derby of the Valencian region: Levante (17th, 11 pts) host Elche (18th, 10 pts), one point apart, with Elche in the drop zone after defeats to Valencia and Betis and without a win at the Ciutat de València in 33 years. Levante have kept no clean sheet in their last five home games; Brugué (5 goals) leads their attack and left-back Manu Sánchez is back from a hamstring problem. Martín Anselmi's Elche keep the ball and cross a lot for Fer Niño (6 goals); Marc Aguado (ankle) is out until mid-December, Lemar, Villar and Sangaré are reported close to fit but not certain, and Houary and Yago Santiago have knocks. The numbers list no missing players for this game and do not flag it as a derby; no referee has been named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.9 goals, already high for two bottom-four sides, because Levante concede a lot at home and Elche create plenty. A tense six-pointer could make both sides careful, but Levante have not kept a home clean sheet in five and Elche's Aguado has been out for a month, so his absence is already in their recent form. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay at 2.9.

Anselmi's Elche keep the ball and lean on crosses to Fer Niño, which the numbers already see in their 31 corners in six games, while Levante have won fewer than expected lately. Nothing new in the team news changes that, so I keep 8.9.

This is a regional derby and a direct relegation fight between two sides a point apart, which the numbers do not flag, and games like that usually bring more fouls and bookings; Levante's Dela and Elche's Gonzalo Villar are one booking from a ban. No referee is named yet, so a clear but moderate lean up to about 4.7.

shots.text: The numbers say 29.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting (Levante conceded 103 in six games). shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.9 shots on target. Brugué and Fer Niño, each side's top scorer, are both fit, and Elche's doubts (Lemar, Houary) are about creators who have missed games already, so their recent output counts it. I keep 8.9.
